title: Customer Operations Program Manager
description:
About Us:

Trilliant Food & Nutrition is a leading manufacturer of premium coffees and powdered beverages, proudly headquartered in Little Chute, Wisconsin. With a legacy rooted in quality, innovation, and service, Trilliant delivers branded and private label solutions across retail, foodservice, and e-commerce channels.

Horseshoe Beverage Company, based in Neenah, WI, is a leading ready-to-drink beverage manufacturer dedicated to delivering an exceptional beverage experience. By combining industry-leading talent and cutting-edge equipment, we drive innovation and consistently deliver the highest quality products to our customers—first and fast.

Our brand portfolio includes Victor Allen’s®, Dutch Bros® beverages and Nurri™, our better-for-you protein beverage line. We are passionate about beverages – and about building a team that’s just as energized. We invite you to explore opportunities at Trilliant or Horseshoe, to see if your talents and career aspirations may fit with our openings.

Our Core Values:

Position Overview:

The Customer Operations Program Manager serves as the strategic operational partner for assigned customers and is accountable for a standardized way of work across customer operational performance, inventory and replenishment insights, service execution, compliance, cost-to-serve visibility, and continuous improvement. The role is aligned to the customer not to a brand portfolio and develops deep knowledge of the customer’s systems, requirements, inventory position, replenishment processes, service expectations, and operational priorities.

The COPM connects customer data and operational signals to action. The role works closely with Sales and cross-functional partners to identify risks and opportunities, provide actionable insights, facilitate root-cause resolution, and ensure clear ownership and follow-through.

For this specific customer assignment, the COPM will support Walmart and Sam’s Club and must bring demonstrated replenishment and customer operational experience supporting both Walmart and Sam’s Club. This role requires deep working knowledge of Walmart and Sam’s Club replenishment processes, systems, inventory and POS data, and customer-specific operational requirements, including hands-on experience with Retail Link and Nova.

Responsibilities:

Customer Operational Partnership

· Develop an intimate understanding of assigned customers, including customer systems, processes, replenishment requirements, service expectations, operational contacts, and business priorities.

· Serve as the primary operational partner for assigned customers in partnership with the Sales account owner.

· Establish a consistent customer operating cadence, including operational/replenishment reviews, KPI reviews, risk and opportunity discussions, action tracking, and escalation.

· Translate customer needs and operational signals into clear actions and connect work to the appropriate internal partner through resolution.

Inventory, Replenishment & POS Analytics

· Monitor and analyze customer POS, store/DC inventory, in-stock levels, weeks of supply, order patterns, MABD/fill-rate compliance, OTIF/service performance, and other customer-specific inventory and replenishment measures.

· Identify out-of-stock risk, excess or imbalanced inventory, replenishment gaps, order opportunities, service risk, and other material customer-operational concerns.

· Perform root-cause analysis and provide actionable recommendations to improve in-stock, inventory flow, replenishment, service, and the cost of moving product optimally.

· Provide order/replenishment recommendations using customer demand signals, inventory position, transit and lead-time considerations, promotions, seasonality, and customer requirements.

· Prepare customer-specific replenishment/performance reporting and lead or participate in recurring customer replenishment meetings.

· Develop and improve replenishment tools, reporting, processes, and standard work as business and customer requirements evolve.

· Serve as the customer operations and replenishment subject-matter expert for Walmart and Sam’s Club, maintaining deep knowledge of customer-specific replenishment processes, systems, metrics, reporting, and operational expectations.

· Utilize Walmart and Sam’s Club systems, including Retail Link and Nova, to analyze POS, store/DC inventory, in-stock performance, replenishment trends, order activity, and other customer-specific operational data.

· Prepare for and lead recurring replenishment and operational performance discussions with Walmart and Sam’s Club replenishment teams, identifying risks, opportunities, root causes, and recommended actions.

Demand & Forecast Insights

· Gather and translate customer POS and/or DC, inventory, replenishment, order, promotional, seasonal, and other customer demand signals into actionable insights for Sales, Demand Planning, and Supply Chain.

· Provide forecast recommendations and proactively identify material changes in demand or inventory position.

· Maintain an active seat at the business table by ensuring customer and replenishment insights inform commercial and operational planning.

Customer Operational Performance

· Own visibility to customer operational KPIs, including OTIF, in-stock, MABD/fill rate, inventory position/weeks of supply, replenishment performance, service performance, compliance, and applicable cost-to-serve measures.

· Maintain visibility to purchase-order-through-delivery performance and partner with Customer Service, Logistics, Supply Chain, and other functions to identify systemic execution issues.

· Monitor applicable customer compliance requirements, deductions, chargebacks/fines, and recurring operational failures; coordinate root-cause analysis, corrective action, and prevention with cross-functional partners.

· Escalate material risks with clear business/customer impact, ownership, recommended actions, and timing.

· Identify operational drivers impacting customer performance, service, inventory flow, and cost-to-serve, and provide actionable insights and recommendations to Sales and leadership.

Continuous Improvement & Standard Way of Work

· Lead continuous-improvement efforts related to customer operations, replenishment, inventory, service, compliance, data visibility, and cross-functional execution.

· Standardize customer-operational processes, KPI definitions, reporting, meeting cadences, escalation paths, documentation, and action management wherever practical.

· Document root causes, decisions, owners, actions, and outcomes to ensure improvements are sustained.

· Share scalable best practices across customers while maintaining customer-specific system and process requirements.

Cross-Functional Coordination & Accountability

· Partner with Sales, Customer Service, Supply Chain, Demand Planning, Logistics, Finance, Marketing/Ecommerce, Project Management, Master Data, IT/EDI, and other functions as required.

· Coordinate customer-operational dependencies and provide visibility when cross-functional decisions or actions create customer, service, inventory, cost, or execution risk.

· Support cross-functional initiatives from the customer-operations perspective.

Customer & Operational Readiness

· Support new customer and new item operational readiness by documenting and communicating customer systems, service, replenishment, compliance, and operational requirements.

· Partner with the appropriate cross-functional teams to ensure required setup and readiness activities are completed accurately and on time.

· Provide customer-specific operational input to bids, RFPs, launches, and commercial initiatives as requested.

Leadership

· Independently manage complex, high-impact customer operational relationships and issues.

· Exercise judgment in prioritizing risk, developing recommendations, escalating concerns, and driving cross-functional resolution.

· Lead high-impact operational discussions with customers, Sales, and senior leadership.

· Support the development of consistent capabilities, tools, best practices, and standardized ways of working across Customer Operations.

Qualifications:

· Bachelor’s degree in Business, Supply Chain, Operations, Analytics, Marketing, or a related field; equivalent relevant experience may be considered.

· 4–7 years of experience in customer operations, replenishment, retail/customer analytics, customer success, account operations, supply chain, or a related role supporting complex customers.

· Direct replenishment experience supporting both Walmart and Sam’s Club is required, including demonstrated experience analyzing POS, store/DC inventory, in-stock performance, replenishment, MABD/fill-rate compliance, order patterns, and customer-specific operational performance.

· Hands-on experience with Walmart and Sam’s Club systems, including Retail Link and Nova, is required, with demonstrated ability to independently navigate customer data, reporting, inventory, POS, and replenishment information.

· Experience with additional Walmart and Sam’s Club systems and tools, including Madrid, Scintilla, ASPEN, Supplier One, and other applicable customer platforms, is highly preferred.

· Strong analytical capability with demonstrated ability to interpret POS, inventory, replenishment, service, compliance, and operational data and convert findings into actionable recommendations.

· Strong Excel skills and ability to work effectively with customer portals, retailer/replenishment systems, ERP/customer systems, reporting tools, and large data sets.

· Strong customer-facing communication and relationship-building skills.

· Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional problem solving without direct authority and drive actions through completion.

· Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, ownership, intellectual curiosity, and ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced environment.

· Travel is required based on customer needs and business objectives.

Hours, Location and Pay:

We offer a competitive base pay rate and benefits package for full-time employees. This role works standard business hours Monday – Friday with additional hours as needed to support business needs. If working remotely, travel to our Little Chute, WI manufacturing facility will occasionally be required. Additional travel as needed based on customer needs.

Physical and Mental Demands:

· While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to sit, hear, use hands to type data, use a personal computer and telephone. This employee may occasionally have to operate business machines and lift and/move up to 50 pounds.

· Specific vision abilities required in this job include close vision and the ability to adjust focus. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

· Mental demands include multi-tasking, decision making, problem solving, comparing, copying, computing, compiling, analyzing, coordinating, and synthesizing data.

· Potential for exposure to chemicals, heights, loud noises, mechanical equipment, wet environments, and other potential hazards exists.

Safety Statement:

At Trilliant and Horseshoe, safety is every employee’s first responsibility. We expect all employees to adhere to all safety practices, have the moral courage to stop other individuals from performing unsafe acts, and immediately report unsafe conditions.

Disclosures:

· The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by people assigned to this classification. They are not to be construed as an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, and skills required of personnel so classified. All personnel may be required to perform duties outside of their normal responsibilities from time to time, as needed.

· Responsible for following food safety/regulatory policies and procedures, executing responsibilities as identified in standard operating procedures, and reporting food safety/regulatory concerns to the Production or Quality Manager.

· Trilliant Food & Nutrition and Horseshoe Beverage Company are Drug Free Workplaces. All applicants are subject to a drug screen and background check as a condition of employment.

· Trilliant Food and Nutrition and Horseshoe Beverage participate in the E-Verify process.

· EEO/AA including Vets and Disabled

· If you need a reasonable accommodation for any part of the employment process, please contact us by email at HR@trilliantfood.com and let us know the nature of your request and your contact information.

· Trilliant Food and Nutrition and Horseshoe Beverage are Equal Opportunity Employers.

· The principles of the OECD and UN have been taken into consideration and used as guidance in our human rights practices and procedures.

title: Legal Practice Development Director, Americas
description:
Legal Practice Development Director, Americas

Purpose Statement

sa.global has established a successful Legal Industry business in the UK, with a growing customer base and a proven legal industry solution. The Americas represents the largest legal software market globally and a significant growth opportunity for the business.

The Legal Practice Development Director, Americas is responsible for building and scaling sa.global's Legal Industry presence across Unites States and Canada. The role will lead market development, establish strategic industry partnerships, build executive relationships across the legal sector, and drive the growth of the Legal practice in alignment with the global Legal Industry strategy.

Working closely with the Global Legal Industry Leader, this role will help transfer and scale the success achieved in other markets to the United States and Canada while shaping sa.global's long-term position within the legal industry

Position Overview

The Legal Practice Development Director, Americas will lead the expansion of sa.global's Legal Industry business across the United States and Canada.

Building on the success already achieved in the UK and other markets, the role will focus on establishing sa.global's market presence in the Americas, developing strategic partnerships, building executive relationships across the legal sector, and driving the growth of the Legal practice. The individual will work closely with cross-functional teams across sales, marketing, product, partnerships, and delivery to strengthen sa.global's position in the world's largest legal software market.

The role reports to the Global Legal Industry Leader, with a dotted-line relationship to the Americas Managing Director to ensure alignment between the global Legal Industry strategy and regional business objectives.

Areas of Responsibility

1. Industry Strategy

• Develop and execute the Americas Legal Industry growth strategy aligned with sa.global's global Legal Industry vision.

• Identify priority market segments, growth opportunities, industry trends, and emerging market needs.

• Contribute to the long-term development and positioning of the Legal Industry practice across the Americas.

• Provide strategic input to regional and global leadership on market opportunities, competitive dynamics, and industry developments.

2. Partnerships & Alliances

• Develop and manage strategic relationships with Microsoft and key legal technology partners.

• Identify, establish, and grow partnerships that strengthen sa.global's position within the legal ecosystem.

• Build a network of industry advisors, influencers, associations, referral partners, and technology providers.

• Work with partners to create joint go-to-market opportunities and accelerate business growth.

3. Market Development

• Establish and expand sa.global's presence within the United States and Canada legal sector.

• Build executive-level relationships with managing partners, legal operations leaders, CFOs, CIOs, and other senior stakeholders within law firms.

• Drive awareness of sa.global's Legal Industry capabilities, solutions, and value proposition.

• Identify and engage strategic target accounts and key market influencers.

• Support the development of client reference programs and market success stories.

4. Solution Development

• Work closely with Product, Delivery, and Legal Industry leadership to evolve industry-specific solutions and offerings.

• Provide market insight and client feedback to influence solution development and go-to-market strategies.

• Help identify gaps, opportunities, and innovation areas within the Legal Industry portfolio.

• Support the development of repeatable industry solutions, messaging, and value propositions.

5. Thought Leadership

• Represent sa.global at legal industry events, conferences, webinars, and professional forums.

• Contribute to industry content, market positioning, client success stories, and thought leadership initiatives.

• Serve as an ambassador for sa.global within the legal community.

• Maintain visibility within the legal ecosystem and support the development of sa.global's industry reputation.

6. Sales & Growth

• Drive pipeline creation, client acquisition, and revenue growth across the Legal Industry practice.

• Support strategic opportunity pursuit and executive-level client engagement.

• Collaborate with regional sales teams, Microsoft, and partners to expand market opportunities.

• Develop business cases, proposals, presentations, and commercial strategies for strategic opportunities.

• Provide accurate pipeline updates, forecasts, and growth plans to leadership.

• Support commercial negotiations and successful transition from sales to delivery.

Success Measures

• Strategic partnerships established.

• Executive relationships developed across the legal sector.

• Market presence and brand recognition strengthened.

• Qualified legal pipeline created.

• New legal clients acquired.

• Revenue growth achieved.

• Industry thought leadership established.

• Successful expansion of sa.global's Legal Industry practice across United States and Canada

Skills[PF1.1][ED1.2] and Experience

• Proven experience within the legal industry, legal technology sector, or serving law firms.

• Strong understanding of law firm operations, business models, and industry trends.

• Experience building new markets, industry practices, strategic partnerships, or go-to-market initiatives.

• Established network and credibility within the legal ecosystem.

• Demonstrated ability to build relationships with senior executives and industry stakeholders.

• Commercially minded with experience driving business growth, pipeline development, and revenue generation.

• Demonstrated success in business development, strategic sales, or revenue growth within the legal industry or legal technology sector.

• Strong communication, influencing, presentation, and relationship-building skills.

• Ability to lead and influence cross-functional teams without direct authority.

• Self-motivated, entrepreneurial, and comfortable operating in a growth-oriented environment.

• Willingness and ability to travel throughout United States and Canada.

title: Physical Therapy Technician
description:
Current Saint Francis Employees - Please click HERE to login and apply.

This position is ECB status – requires a minimum number of worked hours per month as needed by the department; limited benefit offerings.

Days

Hours: 7:30am to 3:30pm

Must be able to work weekends

Job Summary: Assists with direct patient care as directed by RPT/RPTA. Performs treatment procedures (gait, exercises, ROM) as appropriate. Assists with patient transfers and bed mobility. Assists therapist with getting necessary equipment needed during patient treatment.

Minimum Education: High School Diploma or GED.

Licensure, Registration and/or Certification: None.

Work Experience: 0 - 6 months related experience.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities: Effective interpersonal, oral and written communication skills.

Essential Functions and Responsibilities: Assists with direct patient care as directed by RPT/RPTA. Performs treatment procedures (gait, exercises, ROM) as appropriate. Assists with patient transfers and bed mobility. Applies and knows contraindications for mobility use. Assists therapist with getting necessary equipment needed during patient treatment. Provides procedural assistance by: verifying with nurse for contraindications before patient treatment. Calls around to assist others when own (Attendant and Physical Therapist) patient load done or P.T. no longer needs his/her assistance. Performs departmental assistance by: Assisting with W/P patient transporting and stocking of laundry. Performs stocking of crutches and/or filling oxygen tanks on one-month rotation basis. Willingly assists and/or changes partners as needed during rotations. Prepares treatment area or patient environment by: When appropriate, shows patient to booth, provides gown, and helps maintain patient's modesty. Arranges IV lines, Foley, and patient's chair in preparation for patient treatment. When appropriate, fills patient's ice bag, replaces patient's call light and table, and puts patient's rails up. Maintains education level by: Attends 95% of scheduled monthly in- services and departmental meetings. Through departmental in-services or one-on-one education, learns new treatment techniques or the use of modalities. Serves as example for new attendants and provides information on the 'why' behind specific techniques and modalities. Cleans and assists in the maintenance of outpatient equipment. Assures the department/equipment is clean, prior to and following treatments.

Decision Making: Independent judgment in making minor decisions where alternatives are limited and standard policies/protocols have been established.

Working Relationships: Works directly with patients and/or customers. Works with internal customers via telephone or face to face interaction. Works with external customers via telephone or face to face interaction. Works with other healthcare professionals and staff.

Special Job Dimensions: None.

title: IT Support Analyst
description:
Floorplan Xpress is a national leader in the automotive finance industry. We are looking for an IT Support Analyst in our Norman, OK Operations Center. This position is in-office, Monday-Friday.

The IT Support Analyst will be responsible for providing technical assistance and support to Floorplan Xpress users while providing excellent customer service. In operation since 1974, our independently owned organization takes pride in living our mission, to empower independent auto dealers with the financing solutions they need to acquire the vehicles that drive their business forward. title: Railroad Signal Technician
description:
Signal Maintainer - Madison, WI area

Incentives Include:

  • Company vehicle, laptop, and cell phone provided.
  • Wages are negotiable as per experience.

Benefits Include:

  • Health, dental, vision, and 401-K plan.
  • Employer paid long term disability and life insurance for all full-time employees.
  • Paid holidays after 60 days of employment.
  • Employee referral bonuses
Summary
A Railroad Signal Maintainer for CDL is responsible for testing, maintaining and improving signal systems at grade crossings and way-side signal locations in accordance with FRA and CDL standards. Alacrity, Dependability, Pride, Ownership, Teamwork and having a Safety Mindset are the hallmarks of a top performer in this job class.
A signal maintainer will be evaluated in 5 basic areas:
  • Safety
  • Maintenance & Improvements
  • Testing & Inspections
  • Trouble Calls & Troubleshooting
  • Team Player

Preferred Experiences:

  • Knowledge of basic electronics and electrical fundamentals with an emphasis in low-voltage AC & DC circuits and relay or ladder logic. Must be able to read wiring diagrams and use multi-meter.
  • Knowledge of rail operations generally and railroad signaling principals specifically. The focus of a signal maintainer will be grade crossing warning systems, defect detectors and AEI readers and possibly radio communications.
  • Signal maintaining is a largely independent job thus good time management and personal initiative are essential.
  • Must be proficient with a personal computer and the MS Office line of products.
  • High school diploma or GED equivalent unless otherwise approved by upper management.
  • Relatable experience in HVAC, Avionics, Communications, Motor Control and PLCs will also be evaluated as requirements for the job. Responsible for testing, maintaining, and improving grade crossing warning, AEI, or defect detector systems on an assigned territory. Follow regulations and testing procedures as set forth in the Blue Book.
  • Willing to be On-Call much of the time and respond to dispatch and supervisor Trouble Calls in a timely manner.
  • Understand and comply with FRA rules and regulations around railroad signaling, including the Hours-of-Service Law.
  • Be responsible for all paperwork and retention schedules. Paperwork can include testing records, HOS forms, timesheets, material handling forms and trouble tickets. The responsibility for complete and accurate testing records and HOS documentation may continue after separation from CDL; voluntary or involuntary.
  • Foster good relationships with local railroad customers and supplier.
  • Be a team player willing to help on other territories and railroads. Assist with special projects, when assigned.
  • Responsible for the safety of themselves and those around them. Reports any unsafe conditions that may exist.
  • Keep company vehicle, equipment, tools and meters in good working order, following all maintenance and calibration schedules.
  • Responsible for implementing strategies to maximize profitability in their area of responsibility.
  • Other duties assigned by leadership team.
  • Demonstrate and attain CDL Core Values: SAFETY, PEOPLE, INTEGRITY, ACCOUNTABILITY, AND EXCELLENCE
  • Demonstrate and attain CDL Core Focus: CUSTOMER SERVICE

Physical Demands:

  • Standing, walking, bending, kneeling and/or sitting for long periods of time.
  • Climbing ladders to reach ceilings and other high objects.
  • Push/Pull/Lift/Moving 50 pounds repeatedly.
  • Working in adverse weather conditions.
  • Walk and stand on uneven surfaces.

title: Family Programming Attendant-Bob Sierra Family YMCA

This position is responsible for providing safe and enjoyable childcare for members and their children by maintaining visual and auditory supervision at all times. Attendants are responsible for the safety and well-being of each child under their supervision and will provide engagement and direction to a large group of children varying in age and ability. In addition, attendants will exhibit behaviors and attitudes that are consistent with the YMCA Mission and policies of the association.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Demonstrate enthusiasm and a passion for working with children of all ages and abilities
  • Communicate in a professional and positive manner to children, parents, guests, and other associates
  • Provide a safe and enjoyable environment for members and their children
  • Greet every parent and child as they arrive and depart from the area and ensures that parents/guardians follow the sign in/sign out procedures for drop off and pick up according to Y policies/procedures
  • Engage children by implementing curriculum, thematic discussions, arts and crafts activities, and best practices daily
  • Initiate and supervise age appropriate games and activities
  • Maintain a clean environment by disinfecting toys, wiping tables and chairs, wiping shelves, putting toys and equipment away properly, cleaning common areas, and wiping bathrooms and sinks down as necessary
  • Maintain a safe environment by directly supervising children throughout the program area – encouraging positive behaviors, knowing where each child is at all times and never leaving a child unattended, maintaining the sign in/sign out sheet, identifying potential hazards in the area, and adhering to Y policies and s
  • Follow standards and policies as explained in the Family Programming Staff Handbook, the Parent Manual, and the Tampa YMCA Employee Handbook
  • Enforce all rules and make effective decision making to assure the safety and security of program participants
  • Facilitate group games, activities, and arts and crafts during the Parent’s Night Out program
  • Set up and clean up for the Parent’s Night Out event
  • Perform general housekeeping tasks; maintains clean and safe are
  • Apply YMCA policies and procedures, including those related to medical and disciplinary situations, child abuse prevention, and emergency procedures including serving as a mandated reporter
  • Attend staff meetings and training programs, as required
  • Exhibit behaviors and attitudes that are consistent with the YMCA Mission and policies of the association
  • Perform all other duties as assigned

Education/ Experience Required:

  • Must be at least 15 years of age; 16 years of age preferred
  • High School Diploma or GED preferred
  • Preferred but not required: School, community, volunteer, or work experience requiring interaction with children

Certifications/Trainings Required:

  • Must obtain within 30 days of employment and maintain current certifications in CPR, AED, and First Aid
  • Complete required Stay and Play trainings within first 30 days of employment
  • Must successfully complete Level 2 fingerprinting - for more information, click the link ( )
  • Must successfully complete all Child Abuse Prevention trainings as required upon hire and before working in program area
  • Maintain and complete other required certifications as assigned.

WORK ENVIRONMENT AND PHYSICAL DEMANDS:

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job includes, but not limited to:

  • The employee needs sufficient strength, agility and mobility to perform essential functions and to supervise program activities in a wide variety of indoor and outdoor locations.
  • While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to use a computer for extended periods of time and be able to communicate using a computer and authorized work phone/smart device.
  • Ability to instruct and observe participants during program activities.
  • The employee frequently is required to see, observe, and hear all participants, and make sound judgments and decisions.
  • Ability to perform all physical aspects of the position, including, but not limited to, leading class, walking, standing, bending, reaching, and lifting.
  • Ability to sit and reach, and must be able to move around the work environment.
  • Hear noises and distress signals in the program environment, including in the classroom and anywhere around the zone of responsibility.
  • Must have flexibility and the ability to adapt to changing circumstances.
  • Ability to lift and move a minimum of 30 pounds.
  • Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus.
  • Ability to work in a variety of environments, specifically those subject to extreme humidity/dampness, heat and cold.
  • The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate to high.
  • This position requires reliable transportation and willing to travel, if needed.

This position may require availability to work flexible hours including evenings, weekends, and holidays as needed.

title: AI Response Evaluator
description:
Available only for: France, Norway, Japan, Mexico, Turkey and Vietnam

About the job iMerit is looking for detail oriented analysts to evaluate and rank AI generated responses to image based prompts. You will judge answers on accuracy, relevance, clarity, conciseness, safety, localization, and how well they follow the user’s instructions, then explain your reasoning in writing. Much of the job comes down to this: look at the image, look at what the model said about it, and decide whether the two actually match.

What you will do:

Interpret conversational context and identify what the user really wanted Rate and rank responses against defined quality criteria Compare multiple answers and explain in writing why one wins Verify factual claims using approved research sources Flag tasks that cannot be reliably assessed rather than guessing

What you bring: Strong critical thinking and sound judgment in ambiguous cases Solid research skills and attention to detail Excellent reading comprehension Professional written English that is clear and concise Self direction and the discipline to hit deadlines without supervision Prior experience in AI evaluation, annotation, writing, editing, research, or translation is a plus, though not required.

Good to know: Independent contractor engagement for the length of the project. Fully remote and flexible. You choose your hours as long as volume and deadlines are met. Task volume varies with project demand. A paid qualification assessment is required before live work begins.

title: MAC On-Call - MAC - Scarborough Town Center, ON
description:
The Estée Lauder Companies Inc. is one of the world’s leading manufacturers, marketers, and sellers of quality skin care, makeup, fragrance, and hair care products, and is a steward of luxury and prestige brands globally. title: Junior Construction Surveillance Technician (Jr CST)
description:
CenCore is seeking a Junior Construction Surveillance Technician (Junior CST) to support secure manufacturing, production, and construction-related activities in Aurora, CO. This role supports the protection of controlled work areas, materials, personnel, and production activities for portable and modular Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities (SCIFs). The Junior CST helps monitor site activity, support access control, document observations, and escalate concerns in accordance with security procedures, construction standards, ICD 705 expectations, and approved project requirements. This is a strong opportunity for a dependable cleared professional with foundational construction security, physical security, or secure-site monitoring experience.

Key Responsibilities

  • Monitor secure manufacturing, production, and construction-related activities to support compliance with security protocols, project specifications, and approved requirements.
  • Support access control processes by observing personnel movement and helping ensure only authorized individuals enter controlled or restricted work areas.
  • Observe contractors, vendors, materials, tools, equipment, work areas, and activity zones for potential security, safety, or compliance concerns.
  • Document and report suspicious activity, procedural violations, safety concerns, process deviations, and other issues through the appropriate reporting channels.
  • Maintain accurate daily logs, observation notes, incident records, visitor documentation, and other required site security records.
  • Conduct routine checks of assigned areas, materials, and activity zones to support secure production, construction security, and site compliance requirements.
  • Coordinate professionally with site security, manufacturing, production, construction, logistics, engineering, quality, and program personnel to support mission continuity.
  • Provide timely updates to site leadership and security personnel regarding observed risks, site status, and follow-up actions.
  • Follow site safety protocols, personal protective equipment requirements, and secure manufacturing expectations at all times.

Required Qualifications

  • U.S. citizenship required.
  • Ability to provide a valid U.S. Passport Book or Passport Card.
  • Active security clearance required; clearance level must be confirmed based on contract and customer requirements.
  • High school diploma or equivalent required.
  • Minimum of 1 year of experience in Construction Surveillance Technician (CST), construction security, secure facility, physical security, access control, site monitoring, military security, industrial security, or a related field.
  • Foundational understanding of security protocols, access control, visitor control, escort requirements, and secure construction or production practices.
  • Ability to observe and document work activity, personnel movement, materials, tools, equipment, and potential security or safety concerns.
  • Strong attention to detail, sound judgment, and effective verbal and written communication skills.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a cross-functional team in a secure manufacturing or construction-like environment.
  • Ability to use communication devices, reporting systems, access logs, surveillance tools, and related site security technology.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Current Department of State Construction Surveillance Technician certification or CenCore-approved CST training.
  • Experience supporting portable or modular SCIF production, SCIF construction, secure facility manufacturing, controlled area operations, or cleared construction projects.
  • Familiarity with ICD 705, TEMPEST-related requirements, technical surveillance risk mitigation, SCIF construction, modular secure facilities, or secure production processes.
  • Experience supporting government contracts, defense, intelligence community, critical infrastructure, secure manufacturing, or cleared work environments.
  • First Aid, CPR, AED, OSHA, construction safety, or related certifications.
  • Active Secret, Top Secret, or TS/SCI clearance, if aligned with customer requirements.

Skills / Competencies

  • Construction security awareness and situational judgment.
  • Observation, inspection support, and issue escalation.
  • Accurate documentation, report writing, and recordkeeping.
  • Professional communication with security, construction, production, and program stakeholders.
  • Attention to detail in controlled or sensitive environments.
  • Ability to follow post orders, site procedures, and customer security requirements.
  • Reliability, discretion, and accountability when handling sensitive information.
  • Ability to support safe, compliant operations in active work environments.

Work Environment and Physical Requirements

  • Work is performed on-site in a secure manufacturing, production, or construction-like environment in Aurora, CO.
  • Position requires regular monitoring of work areas, controlled spaces, personnel, materials, tools, and equipment.
  • Must be able to stand, walk, observe activity, and move through active production or construction areas for extended periods.
  • May be exposed to noise, dust, machinery, tools, materials, uneven surfaces, and other active-site conditions.
  • Must wear required personal protective equipment and follow all site safety, security, access control, and customer requirements.
  • Schedule may vary based on production activity, construction activity, security coverage needs, customer direction, or mission requirements.
  • Travel is expected to be minimal unless otherwise directed by the program or customer.

title: Hydro Technician Weekend shift
description:
Hayden Industrial, a leading manufacturer of industrial cooling systems, is seeking a Hydro Testing Technician to join our team. The Hydro Testing Technician is responsible for conducting hydrostatic pressure testing on heat exchanger bundles and related assemblies to ensure integrity and compliance with engineering and safety standards. This role requires mechanical aptitude, attention to detail, and a strong commitment to safety protocols.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Perform hydrostatic (hydro) testing on bundle assemblies in accordance with company procedures, ASME standards, and customer specifications.
  • Set up and operate hydro testing equipment including pumps, gauges, valves, and fittings.
  • Read and interpret engineering drawings, test procedures, and pressure specifications.
  • Inspect components visually using measuring devices to detect leaks, deformation, or other defects post-test.
  • Maintain accurate test records, logs, and reports for quality documentation and traceability.
  • Communicate test results with Quality Control and Engineering teams.
  • Perform routine maintenance and calibration of test equipment.
  • Adhere to safety protocols, including lockout/tagout, PPE, and pressure safety practices.
  • Assist with the assembly and preparation of bundles for testing.
  • Collaborate with other team members to ensure timely and high-quality production output.
  • Identify and report non-conforming parts or assemblies.

Hayden Industrial has determined this position involves safety-sensitive job duties and will be considered a safety-sensitive position for purpose of the Oklahoma Medical Marijuana and Patient Protection Act (“The Unity Bill.”) effective August 29th, 2019.

Education and Experience:

  • High School Diploma or GED required.
  • 1–3 years of experience in industrial manufacturing or pressure testing preferred.
  • Familiarity with hydrostatic testing procedures and mechanical systems.
  • Ability to read and interpret technical documents, schematics, and blueprints.
  • Basic understanding of pressure ratings, fluid dynamics, and testing principles.
  • Proficient with hand tools and mechanical equipment.
  • Strong attention to detail and documentation accuracy.
  • Forklift certification is a plus.
  • ASME Code knowledge or certification (Section VIII / Pressure Vessels) is a plus.

Supervisor Responsibility:
This position has no supervisory responsibilities.

Work Environment:
Non-temperature-controlled environment with loud noises, dust, dirt, and metal particles that are usually associated with metal fabrication shops. All employees are required to wear personal protective equipment to include noise/hearing protection, safety glasses with side shields, (paint masks, respirator, when required) and OSHA compliant safety boots/shoes within the manufacturing facility.

Physical Demands:
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job.

While performing duties of this job, the employee in this position is regularly required to stand for long periods of time. This position requires walking, the ability to reach, ascend/descend ladders, bend, kneel, and stoop. The employee occasionally will lift and/or move up to 50 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception and ability to adjust focus.

Position Type/Expected Hours of Work:
This is a full-time position. Days and hours of work are Friday through Sunday, 5:00 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. Occasional evening and weekday work may be required as job duties demand.

Travel:
No travel is required for this position.

Benefits:
Hayden Industrial offers a generous benefits package including comprehensive health, dental, vision, 401(k) retirement plan with company match, a generous paid time off schedule, and professional development opportunities.

AAP/EEO Statement:
Hayden Industrial is an equal employment opportunity employer. Hayden Industrial recognizes and embraces federal legislation on equal employment opportunity and is committed to providing a workplace free of discrimination. All applicants for employment and all employees will be afforded equal opportunity and treatment, regardless of age, race, religion, gender, national origin, disability status or other protected status. All employees are responsible for complying with all applicable Federal, State and Local Laws, rules and regulations regarding non-discrimination practices.

Job Type: Full-time

Benefits:

  • 401(k)
  • 401(k) matching
  • Dental insurance
  • Employee assistance program
  • Flexible spending account
  • Health insurance
  • Life insurance
  • Paid time off

People with a criminal record are encouraged to apply

Education:

Experience:

  • pressure testing: 1 year (Preferred)

title: Development Officer
company: The Baker Center for Children and Families
description:
Development Officer

Job Title: Development Officer

Location: Waltham, On-site with opportunity for hybrid schedule

Position Type: Full-Time

Summary of position:

The Baker Center for Children and Families (also known as Judge Baker Children's Center), promotes the best possible mental health of children and families through the integration of research, intervention, training, and policy.

The Development Officer helps build, strengthen, and grow our individual giving program by developing relationships with donors and stakeholders across the giving pipeline, including those with the potential to become major donors over time The Development Officer helps create and execute strategy, conducts donor research, supports individual giving and leadership giving engagement efforts through research and collateral development, and engages directly with donors to create opportunities for giving and share compelling stories about the organization and our work. This requires building strong partnerships with program team members and developing a deep understanding of The Baker Center's mission and impact.

The Development Officer also grows our broader individual giving programs, including the fall appeal, Giving Tuesday, and spring appeal, and plays an active role in donor-facing events such as house parties, the gala, and the golf tournament. The role contributes to event strategy, partners with the Development Associate on execution, and participates in key committees.

The Development Officer works independently, is detail-oriented and thorough, and is comfortable making asks and being accountable for results. They are flexible, take initiative, and are willing to contribute across a growing team where responsibilities and priorities may evolve. The Development Officer is an important part of the team responsible for helping the department reach this year's goal of just over $1 million in revenue, a starting point for a program we expect to grow significantly in the years ahead.

What’s in it for me?

  • Make a meaningful impact: Build relationships with donors and help connect their generosity to work that improves the mental health and well-being of children and families.
  • Build and shape a program: Play a meaningful role in growing The Baker Center’s individual giving program and developing its future major donor pipeline.
  • Grow your fundraising career: Gain hands-on experience across donor cultivation, solicitation, stewardship, prospect research, annual giving, and fundraising events.
  • Own your work and see results: Manage meaningful donor relationships, take initiative, and work toward clear goals with measurable impact.
  • Work closely with leadership: Partner directly with the Vice President of Philanthropy and senior staff on donor strategy and major gift engagement.
  • Join a growing team: Bring your ideas, take on new challenges, and contribute across a dynamic Development team as the department continues to grow.
  • Contribute to a shared goal: Be part of the team working toward our current $1 million revenue goal that supports The Baker Center’s mission and programs.

Essential duties:

  • Manages and grows a portfolio of individual donors and prospects across giving levels, with responsibility for cultivation, solicitation, stewardship, and retention.
  • Pursues opportunities to strengthen donor acquisition, retention, renewal, upgrades, recurring giving, and long-term donor engagement.
  • Develops individualized donor strategies using moves management principles, philanthropic interests, giving history, capacity, and engagement opportunities.
  • Conducts personalized outreach, including calls, emails, and meetings, to build authentic relationships and strengthen donor engagement.
  • Conducts prospect research to assess individual donors' philanthropic interests and giving capacity
  • Partners with the Vice President of Philanthropy and senior staff on cultivation and solicitation strategies and collateral development (briefing materials, proposals, and other cultivation resources).
  • Develops annual work plans and fundraising strategies aligned with organizational priorities and revenue objectives.
  • Generates and analyzes fundraising reports to evaluate individual giving activity, campaign performance, portfolio progress, and revenue against goals.
  • Partners with colleagues across The Baker Center to strengthen organization wide leadership, giving engagement and foster a culture of philanthropy.
  • Supports the planning and execution of donor engagement and fundraising events, including logistics coordination, vendor communication, and on-site event management.
  • Works on special projects and contributes to department-wide initiatives and organizational priorities as needed.

Qualifications

Education:

  • Bachelor's degree preferred.
  • Equivalent professional experience in fundraising, philanthropy, development, or a related field may be considered in lieu of a degree.

Experience:

  • 3-5 years of progressive nonprofit development or fundraising experience, with demonstrated responsibility for donor cultivation, solicitation, stewardship, and/or portfolio management.
  • Direct hands-on experience personally soliciting gifts and building donor relationships (calls, meetings, in-person cultivation).
  • Experience in setting measurable fundraising targets and tracking progress through reporting and analysis.
  • Proficiency with Salesforce or another donor/customer relationship management (CRM) system, salesforce preferred.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, particularly Excel, Word, and PowerPoint.

title: Director of Training
description:
Air New England is looking for a full time Director of Training. We are looking for someone who pays attention to detail, has a deep knowledge of the training regulations, and is easy to collaborate with. The Director of Training will report to the Chief Pilot for the efficient and timely training of Air New England flight crewmembers.

Duties include, but may not be limited to:

  • Under the supervision of the Chief Pilot will work to coordinate training activities and training programs to interface with both ground and flight training activities, and also collaborate with other operations team members as needed.
  • Monitoring the training program to comply with FARs and Operations Specifications.
  • Makes recommendations to the Chief Pilot to improve and/or amend the training program as necessary to ensure FAR compliance and maintain the highest safety standard.
  • Continually monitor the validity and assure the quality through adherence to the curriculum and lesson plans of the training process, as it relates to pilot competency at the completion of a training cycle.
  • Liaison with outsource training providers to include oversight of the simulators, ground school hardware and courseware.
  • Maintains the training records of all flight crewmembers, including PRD.
  • Provides notification to the Chief Pilot and operations as it pertains to the individual being assigned duties.
  • This position may include some flying (training flights, checkrides for example).
  • QUALIFICATIONS REQUIRED:
  • Have previous experience in both ground & flight training activities utilizing multi-engine aircraft.
  • Demonstrate proficiency and ease in the classroom and the cockpit environment.
  • Have the ability to determine the performance level of a student.
  • Good written and oral communication skills
  • Experienced, easy to get along with candidates are preferred.

Benefits include 8 paid holidays, Anthem Medical (Includes Vision), HSA, 401K after 90 days of employment, $15,000 company paid life insurance, Company paid short-term disability coverage, 80 hours paid vacation (accrued weekly at 1.53 hours per week), Up to 56 hours of paid sick time (accrued at 1 hour per every 30 hours worked).

title: Field Construction Intern
description:
About Us:

The Garrett Companies is a full-service multifamily development, construction, and property management team with offices in Denver (CO), Indianapolis (IN), and Nashville (TN).

We develop, build, and manage multifamily projects in 22 states — working together at every level to become the most successful multifamily developers in the country. Our superior strategies and award-winning culture span across 18,000+ apartments to date, and our expert trend forecasting helps us deliver living options that quickly find success in their unique markets. To make living and investing in our properties even better, we pair that expertise with mixed-use, retail, office, and restaurant development through trusted partners and in-house brands.

At The Garrett Companies, we are passionate about turning visions into reality! As leaders in the multifamily industry, we pride ourselves in creating communities that positively impact the markets we are in, and our residents can proudly call home.

What You’ll Be Doing:

As a Field Construction Intern, you’ll be fully immersed into on-site construction activities, gaining practice experience and an in-depth understanding of multifamily construction projects. You will work closely with the best in the industry, assisting in various aspects of project execution and site management, while contributing to the successful completion of the project.

Major Objectives:

  • · Gain Hands-On Experience: Develop practical skills by participating in day-to-day construction activities and site operations on multifamily projects. Assist with the execution of various site-specific tasks, which will include a range of duties such as punch list creation and completion and site maintenance – no two days are the same!
  • · Understand Project Lifecycle: Learn about the full lifecycle of multifamily construction projects, from initial planning and site preparation to final inspection and project completion.
  • · Enhance Safety Awareness: Promote job-site safety, encourage safe work practices, and rectify any job site hazards immediately.
  • · Team Collaboration: Maintain positive relationships will all Garrett Companies personnel, including the entire project team, subcontractors, suppliers, and all applicable municipal representatives.

Specific Duties & Responsibilities:

  • · Support Project Team: Actively complete on-site tasks as assigned to achieve completion of the project on schedule and within budget. See how the project evolves and stay on track with required specifications.
  • Maintain an organized job site and site construction office.
  • Foster a positive work environment to provide an opportunity for professional growth and development of employees.

What We’re Looking For:

You are driven, actively demonstrating your willingness to learn from both from the internship program curriculum and from the team of professionals you will work alongside. You are:

  • A Passionate Learner: Eager to learn about project management and construction – bring your enthusiasm and curiosity!
  • A Team Player: Ability to collaborate effectively with others – teamwork is essential in the construction industry.
  • Detail-Oriented: Strong attention to detail and organizational skills – accuracy matters in project management.
  • Have a Proactive Attitude: Self-motivated and proactive – take initiative and contribute positively to the team.

Educational Background:

· Currently enrolled in a Bachelor’s or Master’s Degree in Construction, Construction Management, or relevant field of study.

Skills for Success:

  • · Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite.
  • · Must be an excellent verbal and written communicator.
  • · Ability to handle multiple tasks and for multiple projects.
  • · Ability to work independently and with a team of professionals as needed.

Prerequisites (these are the most important items):

  • Positive attitude.
  • Relentless problem-solving skills.
  • Will never claim the work of others as their own.
  • We are trend setters and standards breakers. Our intent is to consistently surprise our audiences by being excellent.
  • Ability to anticipate.
  • Understanding the difference between causation and correlation.
  • We are all broom pushers. Every member of our team is willing to work and support at all levels.

Perks of the Internship:

  • · Real-World Experience
  • · Mentorship: Learn from industry experts and build relationships that will help facilitate your career.
  • · Growth and Learning: At The Garrett Companies, we believe that Culture = People. That’s why we provide an array of opportunities for our interns to grow as individuals, including applicable learning opportunities, professional development, and more.

title: Security & Fire Alarm Install/Service Technician
description:

At Doyle Security Systems, we offer competitive pay, strong benefits, and the opportunity to build a career in the life-safety and security industry. Our Erie branch serves customers across the southern New York and northwestern Pennsylvania region, including Dunkirk and Erie. This is a versatile, dual-function role. You’ll split your time roughly equally between installing new systems and servicing existing ones, making it ideal for a well-rounded technician who thrives in both environments.

Key Responsibilities:


As a Security & Fire Alarm Installation/Service Technician, you will install and configure new systems as well as troubleshoot, repair, and maintain existing security and life-safety systems across residential and commercial environments in the Dunkirk/Erie corridor.

  • Install, program, and configure electronic security systems including intrusion, fire alarm, video surveillance (CCTV) and live video monitoring systems, access control, and intercom systems
  • Run and terminate low-voltage wiring; install devices including keypads, cameras, sensors, panels, and access control hardware
  • Troubleshoot, diagnose, and repair system issues; reprogram and replace faulty components
  • Perform routine inspections, testing, and preventative maintenance of fire alarm systems in accordance with applicable codes and standards
  • Deliver exceptional customer care on every visit; guide customers through system operation in a clear, professional, and approachable way
  • Accurately document all work activity, including photos, and upload records to customer accounts through company systems

  • 2+ years of experience in low-voltage security or fire alarm systems, with exposure to both installation and service preferred (trainees with strong aptitude considered)
  • Valid driver’s license with a good driving record
  • Experience with security, fire alarm, video surveillance (CCTV) and live video monitoring systems, access control, or intercom systems
  • Strong troubleshooting, diagnostic, and mechanical aptitude
  • Strong communication and customer service skills
  • Ability to work independently and manage both installations and service calls

Work Requirements:

  • Ability to lift equipment and tools as needed
  • Adherence to all safety protocols
  • Willingness to travel daily within the Dunkirk/Erie region; company vehicle provided for business use

Personal Traits:

  • Problem-solver with strong attention to detail

  • Parental leave

  • Tuition reimbursement
  • Employee discount & referral bonus

title: Childwatch Counselor-Foster
description:
Join a team that's creating positive experiences for children and families.

At the YMCA, we're more than a fitness center; we're a community dedicated to strengthening families and supporting youth. As a Childwatch Counselor, you'll play an important role in providing a safe, welcoming, and engaging environment for children while their parents or guardians participate in YMCA programs and services. If you enjoy working with children, creating positive experiences, and helping families feel connected to their YMCA, we'd love to meet you.

What You'll Do

As a Childwatch Counselor, you'll create a fun, safe, and inclusive environment where children can enjoy age-appropriate activities during their time in Childwatch. You'll provide attentive supervision, encourage positive interactions, and help ensure every child and family has a welcoming YMCA experience.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS
1. Supervision and Safety: Ensure the safety and well-being of all children in a welcoming Childwatch environment by monitoring activities to promote safe, age-appropriate behavior and adherence to YMCA policies at all times. Provide for children’s physical needs, including feeding, assisting with restrooms, administering first aid/CPR, and notifying the parents/guardians of necessary diaper changes. Assist with maintaining accurate and up-to-date records such as attendance, incident reports, and compliance documentation. Conduct regular headcounts. Respond promptly and appropriately to emergencies and incidents in alignment with established YMCA protocols and procedures, including emergency preparedness.
2. Behavior Management: Implements positive behavior management techniques that foster a respectful and inclusive environment while addressing the emotional needs of children. Responds to behavioral issues calmly and constructively, following established guidelines, and provides support by soothing distressed children, comforting those who are sick or hurt, redirecting negative behavior, and offering positive reinforcement. Communicates important information or observations to incoming staff regarding individual children and provides an updated list of children currently in attendance.
3. Activity Implementation: Implement a variety of age-appropriate activities, including structured and unstructured activities as outlined in the YMCA-approved curriculum. Encourage and facilitate positive social interactions among children. Adapt activities to meet the diverse needs and interests of all children.
4. Policy Adherence: Follow all organizational policies, protocols, and procedures, including those related to health and safety, child protection, and confidentiality. Maintain a clean and organized environment, adhering to sanitation and safety standards. Report any concerns or issues to the Childwatch Lead or Program Director promptly.
5. Daily Operations. Maintains Childwatch environment by adhering to YMCA of Greater Houston program standards and youth development standards.
6. Leadership: Supervises children under the direction of the Childwatch Lead. Makes sound decisions in alignment with YMCA and youth development standards. Acts as a role model to the children by exemplifying the YMCA’s five core values.
7. Relationship Building: Maintains positive relations with children, parents/guardians, center operations, directors, and other staff. Attends and participates in staff meetings and staff trainings.
8. Administrative Duties: Utilizes designated software to accurately check children in and out of Childwatch. Assist with ensuring tablets and all communication devices are fully charged, ready for use, and properly secured when not in use.
9. Child Abuse Prevention: Report suspicious and inappropriate behaviors and policy violations. Follows mandated abuse and incident reporting requirements. Ensures youth are properly signed in and signed out, ensures only authorized adults are allowed in the facility, etc. Adheres to policies related to boundaries with each child. Ensures unused rooms and closets remain locked; routinely monitors high-risk locations (bathrooms), etc.

QUALIFICATIONS
To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

  • At least 18 years of age.
  • High school diploma or general education degree (GED) preferred.
  • At least 6 months of experience working with youth at a childcare facility, church, school or equivalent (preferred).
  • Strong awareness of child safety and the ability to respond to emergency situations appropriately.
  • Must be able to successfully pass CPR, First Aid, AED certifications and Child Abuse prevention trainings.
  • Ability to engage with children positively and create an environment that fosters learning and respect.
  • Ability to plan, organize, and implement age-appropriate/developmentally appropriate program activities.
  • Previous experience with diverse populations.
  • Current record of tuberculosis examination and/or current local health department regulations, examinations, and/or immunization as required by the local or State Department of Health.
  • Pass a local/state background and FBI fingerprinting check.
  • Team-oriented mindset

Physical & Work Environment Expectations

This is an active, hands-on role that requires standing, walking, bending, reaching, and engaging with children throughout the day. You may occasionally lift up to 50 pounds. Work is primarily indoors with occasional outdoor activities and exposure to active childcare environments, varying noise levels, and routine cleaning products.

Typical Schedule

Part-time schedules are available seven days a week and may include:

  • Morning Shift: 8:00 a.m. – 1:00 p.m.
  • Afternoon Shift: 11:00 a.m. – 4:00 p.m.
  • Evening Shift: 4:00 p.m. – 8:00 p.m.

Schedules may vary based on location and operational needs.

Participation in staff meetings, trainings, family events, and YMCA activities may be required with advance notice.

Why the YMCA

When you join the YMCA, you become part of a mission-driven organization focused on strengthening communities through youth development, healthy living, and social responsibility. As a Childwatch Counselor, you'll help create positive experiences that support families and enhance their YMCA membership experience.

Benefits of Working at the YMCA

  • Free YMCA Membership
  • Discounts on YMCA programs
  • Paid training and professional development opportunities
  • Career growth opportunities within the YMCA
  • Flexible scheduling
  • A supportive, mission-driven team environment
  • Meaningful work that positively impacts children and families

The YMCA of Greater Houston provides Equal Employment Opportunities for employment to all employees and applicants, including disability and protected veteran status.

title: Digital News Producer
description:
The Baltimore Sun is looking for a fast, curious, and highly motivated journalist to help us build a broader and more dynamic daily news report for our readers.

This is a job for someone who loves the news — and loves finding it.

The Digital News Producer will continuously monitor The Sun's network of content partners, news organizations, government agencies and other reliable sources to identify important and compelling stories our readers should know about. The producer will select, edit, aggregate and, when appropriate, build original stories from that material for The Sun's digital platforms and expanded e-edition.

We're looking for someone with excellent news judgment who can move quickly across subjects. On any given day, that might mean identifying a significant investigation from a partner newsroom, spotting a Maryland connection in a national story, turning a government announcement or public document into a clear news story, or recognizing a consequential development being reported elsewhere that The Sun should pursue or include in its report.

The right person will be intellectually curious, competitive and comfortable making decisions. We want someone who looks at a large volume of information and instinctively asks: What's new? What's important? What will our readers care about? And what are we missing?

Essential Functions

  • Monitor The Sun's content partners, including Sinclair, NOTUS, The Epoch Times, The Frederick News Post and other news providers, and identify strong material for publication or further development.
  • Constantly scan other local, regional and national news sources for stories and developments relevant to Sun readers.
  • Select and prioritize stories for an expanded daily e-edition and The Sun's digital report.
  • Write and produce accurate, engaging stories from press releases, public records, government announcements, partner reporting and other appropriately attributed source material.
  • Use AI and other digital tools to accelerate research, discovery and production while independently verifying facts, sources and final copy.
  • Identify Maryland angles and local consequences of important national stories.
  • Rewrite, update, contextualize and package partner material as appropriate under The Sun's agreements and editorial standards.
  • Write strong headlines, summaries and other digital display language.
  • Recognize when a story warrants additional original reporting and alert or work with the appropriate Sun editor or reporter.
  • Maintain high standards for accuracy, attribution, fairness and transparency even while working at speed.
  • Help The Sun experiment with new ways to use partnerships, technology and the breadth of the news ecosystem to give readers a richer daily report.

What we're looking for

  • Strong and independent news judgment.
  • Exceptional curiosity and a broad interest in news, politics, government, crime, business, education, culture and public affairs.
  • The ability to work quickly and accurately across multiple stories and subjects.
  • A competitive instinct and a desire to find important stories before others do.
  • Strong writing, editing and headline-writing skills.
  • Comfort working with material from news organizations with different editorial perspectives and identifying worthwhile journalism regardless of its source.
  • An instinct for accountability journalism and stories involving government performance, public spending, taxes, regulation, public safety and the decisions of powerful institutions.
  • Familiarity with AI-assisted research and production tools, or an eagerness to master them.
  • Sound judgment about sourcing, verification, attribution, copyright and the distinction between confirmed information and claims that require additional reporting.
  • The ability to work independently, prioritize aggressively and produce consistently throughout a shift.

Experience in a digital newsroom, breaking-news operation, local television newsroom, wire service, homepage or audience team is strongly preferred. We care more about speed, judgment, curiosity and demonstrated ability than a particular career path.

This is a hands-on news-production job for a journalist who wants to help determine what The Baltimore Sun covers and put more timely, consequential and interesting journalism in front of our readers every day.

Salary Range: $60,000 – $75,000

Individual compensation may vary from the target range based on several factors, including experience, internal pay equity, and other relevant business consideration.

title: Lähihoitaja vakituiseen työsuhteeseen Lietoon
description:
Lähihoitaja Lietoon Kreivinkotoon – kädet saveen, liikkeelle yhdessä ja musiikki soimaan!

Etsimme lähihoitajaa, joka ei pelkää laittaa itseään likoon – ja välillä laittaa myös musiikin soimaan.

Kuulostaako siltä, että voisit viihtyä meidän porukassamme?

Kreivinkoto Lieto on ikäihmisten yhteisöllinen koti, jossa ei vain hoideta, vaan eletään hyvää arkea yhdessä. Meillä päivä voi sisältää lääkehoitoa ja hoitotyötä, mutta yhtä hyvin myös leivontaa, askartelua, ulkoilua, musiikkia, naurua ja kaikenlaista yhdessä tekemistä.

Etsimme nyt joukkoomme lähihoitajaa, joka haluaa tehdä työtä ihmisten kanssa – ei vain heidän puolestaan.

Mitä työ Kreivinkodossa on?

Olet tärkeä osa asukkaidemme jokapäiväistä elämää. Tuet heidän toimintakykyään, hyvinvointiaan ja itsenäisyyttään sekä olet mukana luomassa mielekästä arkea.

Työhösi kuuluu esimerkiksi:

  • kokonaisvaltaista hoitoa ja huolenpitoa

  • lääkehoitoa

  • asukkaiden ohjaamista ja toimintakyvyn tukemista

  • päivätoiminnan ja yhteisen tekemisen toteuttamista

  • ulkoilua, virikkeitä ja arjen pieniä iloja

  • kohtaamisia asukkaiden ja heidän läheistensä kanssa

  • yhteistyötä muiden ammattilaisten kanssa.

Ja kyllä – välillä tärkein työtehtävä voi olla istua hetkeksi alas, kuunnella ja olla läsnä.

Millainen tyyppi meille sopii?

Toivomme, että olet:

  • koulutukseltasi lähihoitaja

  • lämmin ja helposti lähestyttävä

  • oma-aloitteinen ja vastuuntuntoinen

  • hyvä tyyppi tiimipelaajaksi

  • kiinnostunut ikäihmisten hyvinvoinnista ja hyvästä arjesta

  • valmis tarttumaan tekemiseen ja kokeilemaan uutta.

Sinun ei tarvitse osata kaikkea valmiiksi. Asenne ratkaisee.

Jos tuot mukanasi ripauksen huumoria, hyvät vuorovaikutustaidot ja halun tehdä työsi sydämellä, saatat olla juuri se henkilö, jota etsimme.

Miksi Kreivinkoto?

Koska meillä saat olla lähihoitaja, ihminen ja työkaveri.

Meillä arvostetaan toisiamme ja tehdään töitä yhdessä. Saat mahdollisuuden käyttää omaa osaamistasi monipuolisesti ja olla mukana kehittämässä asukkaidemme arkea.

Meille yhteisöllisyys tarkoittaa sitä, että asukkaat ja työntekijät tekevät arkea yhdessä.

Ja ehkä juuri siksi täällä ei ole kahta samanlaista työpäivää.

Kiinnostuitko?

Jos ajattelet, että tuonne minä haluaisin töihin, älä jää vain ajattelemaan – laita hakemus tulemaan!

Kerro meille lyhyesti itsestäsi ja siitä, miksi juuri sinä sopisit Kreivinkotoon.

Kreivinkodossa hyvä arki ei synny itsestään – tehdään se yhdessä.

Aloitamme haastattelut jo ennen hakuajan päättymistä, joten hae heti, niin päästään tutustumaan. Haluatko osaksi työyhteisöä, jossa kaikilla on tärkeä tehtävä ja halu menestyä yhdessä? Laita hakemuksesi Annelle (anne.holmberg@kototiimi.fi)

Lue meistä lisää www.kototiimi.fi

Summary
A Railroad Signal Maintainer for CDL is responsible for testing, maintaining and improving signal systems at grade crossings and way-side signal locations in accordance with FRA and CDL standards. Alacrity, Dependability, Pride, Ownership, Teamwork and having a Safety Mindset are the hallmarks of a top performer in this job class.
A signal maintainer will be evaluated in 5 basic areas:
  • Safety
  • Maintenance & Improvements
  • Testing & Inspections

  • Team Player

Preferred Experiences:

  • Knowledge of rail operations generally and railroad signaling principals specifically. The focus of a signal maintainer will be grade crossing warning systems, defect detectors and AEI readers and possibly radio communications.

  • Must be proficient with a personal computer and the MS Office line of products.

The responsibility for complete and accurate testing records and HOS documentation may continue after separation from CDL; voluntary or involuntary.
