title: Senior Editor/Page One
description:
The Baltimore Sun is seeking a sharp, ambitious Senior Editor/Page One to help identify, develop and elevate the most consequential journalism produced by our newsroom.

This is a hands-on editing and story-development role for an experienced journalist with exceptional news judgment, strong accountability instincts and the ability to recognize the story others miss.

The Senior Editor/Page One will look across the newsroom each day for journalism worthy of our most prominent digital and print presentation — and help reporters and editors get it there. That means identifying the strongest angle, recognizing missing reporting, developing smart follow-ups and helping turn promising daily stories into distinctive enterprise and accountability journalism.

We want someone who understands that major journalism does not always require months of reporting. A revealing public record, an overlooked government decision, an audit, a contract, a court filing, a contradiction or the right follow-up question can produce consequential journalism in hours or days.

This editor should constantly be asking: What's the real story? What are we missing? Who made this decision? Who benefited? What did it cost? Who is affected? Who should be held accountable? What can we find out today that our competitors don't know?

The Senior Editor/Page One will work across desks to collaborate closely with assignment editors and reporters, direct or assist with major coverage and help establish a newsroom-wide standard of urgency, ambition and accountability.

Essential Functions

  • Identify the strongest journalism across The Sun's daily report and determine which stories have the potential for prominent digital and Page One treatment.
  • Work with reporters and assignment editors to determine what additional reporting, sourcing, documentation, context or framing can elevate promising stories.
  • Recognize important news quickly — including significant developments that may be buried in press conferences, government meetings, reports, audits, budgets, court filings and public records.
  • Find the larger accountability story behind daily developments.
  • Develop quick-turn accountability and investigative work that can be reported in hours or days rather than reserving enterprise journalism for long-term projects.
  • Look for opportunities involving government spending, contracts, taxes, development, public safety, education, regulatory failures, institutional performance, conflicts of interest, promises versus results and other matters of significant public consequence.
  • Ask who made decisions, who benefited, who paid, what went wrong, and whether leaders and institutions delivered what they promised.
  • Help reporters follow money through budgets, contracts, grants, nonprofits, development agreements, campaign finance records, settlements and other public and private spending.
  • Identify reporting holes before publication, including missing records, sources, data, context, responses, relevant history or evidence.
  • Challenge assumptions and official narratives regardless of their source and ensure conclusions are supported by reporting.
  • Help reporters and editors identify meaningful follow-up stories and prevent consequential journalism from becoming one-day coverage.
  • Generate original story ideas and help develop reporting plans for executing them quickly.
  • Edit high-priority stories for reporting, structure, fairness, accuracy, clarity and impact.
  • Assist in directing major breaking news, including determining what can be published immediately, what needs additional verification and what reporters should pursue next.
  • Help coordinate newsroom-wide coverage when major stories cross traditional beats or departments.
  • Work closely with audience, visuals and other newsroom teams to ensure our strongest journalism is presented effectively and reaches the largest appropriate audience.

Page One: Page One is both a specific responsibility and an editorial standard for this position. The Senior Editor/Page One will help select and develop journalism for the print front page while maintaining a digital-first approach.The goal is not simply to assemble Page One, but to help create more journalism worthy of it by identifying promising stories early, strengthening reporting and ensuring our strongest work receives thoughtful presentation across platforms.

AI, Technology and Newsgathering: The Baltimore Sun expects journalists to embrace emerging tools that can make reporting and editing faster, deeper and more effective.The Senior Editor/Page One should be an enthusiastic and responsible adopter of AI-assisted tools and help reporters and editors use them effectively. AI should strengthen journalism, not substitute for reporting, verification or editorial judgment. This editor should understand that distinction and model smart, responsible experimentation.

The strongest candidates will have:

  • Significant professional journalism experience, ideally including both reporting and editing.
  • Exceptional news judgment and the ability to recognize consequential stories quickly.
  • Strong accountability and investigative instincts.
  • Experience working with public records, government documents, data, or other primary-source reporting.
  • Excellent structural and line-editing skills.
  • The ability to diagnose reporting gaps and clearly identify what additional work is needed.
  • Strong breaking-news instincts and comfort making decisions under deadline pressure.
  • A record of generating original journalism rather than relying primarily on scheduled events or outside pitches.
  • Demonstrated curiosity about AI, emerging technology and more efficient approaches to reporting and editing.
  • Strong understanding of sourcing, verification, fairness, attribution and journalistic ethics.
  • Comfort working across beats and with journalists of different experience levels.
  • An understanding of digital publishing, audience behavior and effective story presentation.
  • Urgency, curiosity, competitiveness and intellectual independence.

Salary Range: $85,000 – $110,000

Individual compensation may vary from the target range based on several factors, including experience, internal pay equity, and other relevant business considerations.

title: Site Coordinator- Before and After School Care (Tambark Creek Elementary)
description:

Availability: Monday-Friday; Must be available for shifts between 6:20 a.m. and 6:30 p.m. Site hours are 6:20-9:00am and 3:15-6:30pm M-TH & 2:00-6:30pm Friday.

Make Every Day Matter

At the Y, we believe every child deserves a safe place to belong, caring adults who believe in them, and opportunities to learn, grow, and thrive. As the nation's leading nonprofit dedicated to strengthening communities, we bring people together to build healthy, connected, and resilient communities.

This is more than a job- it's an opportunity to grow your leadership skills, build meaningful relationships, and be part of an organization dedicated to strengthening communities.

If you're passionate about youth development, enjoy leading others, and want a career where your work truly matters, we'd love to have you join the Y team.

What you will do at the Y:

As a Before & After School Site Coordinator, you will lead and oversee the daily operation of a high-quality licensed school-age child care program. You'll lead and support a team of staff, create a safe and engaging environment for children, and build positive relationships with families and school partners.

During the school year, you'll work in our before and after-school programs. During the summer, you'll serve in a leadership role at one of our YMCA day camps.

Work Schedule

This is an in-person, full-time, year-round position working directly with children, Monday-Friday.

Site Coordinators typically work a combination of:

  • Morning program hours before school

  • Administrative hours during the school day

  • Afternoon program hours after school

  • On non-school days and summer breaks: Full Day program hours, 8-hour shift.

Most Site Coordinators work 35-40 hours per week, with a mix of leadership, administrative, and direct program in-ratio responsibilities.

Why Work at The Y?

  • Lead a fun and supportive team.

  • Receive ongoing training and professional development.

  • Grow your career with the YMCA.

  • Be part of an organization that is committed to helping every child and family thrive.

Job Duties/Responsibilities:

  • Lead the daily operations of a licensed before and after-school program.

  • Coordinate with the Program Director to develop, prepare, and implement engaging, age-appropriate activities that promote learning, belonging, and healthy development.

  • Supervision of all children and related program area activities.

  • Supervise, coach, and support a team of youth development staff.

  • Foster a safe, inclusive, and welcoming environment for every child.

  • Build positive relationships with families, school staff, and community partners.

  • Ensure compliance with state and local regulations in addition to YMCA standards and procedures.

  • Maintain materials, equipment, and program facility.

  • Maintain required program records.

  • Complete administrative responsibilities including scheduling, planning, communication, and documentation.

  • Support nearby Y school-age care sites as needed.

  • Performs other duties as assigned.

Qualifications:

  • Minimum age 18, 21 preferred

  • Two or more years working in licensed School-Age Care program, with children in a developmentally appropriate group setting. Preferred, YMCA experience.

  • Meet educational and experience qualifications established by the DCYF (Dept of Children, Youth and Families

  • Have a high school diploma or equivalent;

  • Complete thirty college credits in any one hundred-level or above college coursework or equivalent;

OR

  • Have completed at least twelve college credits in any one hundred-level or above college coursework or equivalent AND complete an additional eighteen college credits in any one hundred-level or above coursework or equivalent within five years of employment

  • Provide documentation of all certification and training requirements established by the DCYF, including position prerequisites, current negative TB test, fully vaccinated for MMR/other required vaccinations*, and portable background check

  • Experience planning, organizing, and implementing high quality developmentally appropriate programming

  • Experience working with individuals, families and communities of diverse backgrounds and abilities

  • Fluency in second language desired

*medical or religious exemptions may be possible

Our Commitment to Inclusion:
The Y is made up of people of all ages and from every walk of life, working side by side to strengthen communities. Together we work to ensure that everyone, regardless of ability, age, cultural background, ethnicity, faith, gender, gender identity, ideology, income, national origin, race or sexual orientation, has the opportunity to reach their full potential with dignity. Our core values are caring, honesty, respect and responsibility—they guide everything we do.

We look forward to having you on our YMCA team.

title: Assembler
description:
Job summary:

Assembles fabricated parts at floor stations. Tests and calibrates parts and mechanisms to meet tolerances and product specifications. Uses hand tools and power tools to assemble units according to product specifications. Identifies units that fail tests or tolerance levels and repairs as necessary. Has knowledge of commonly-used concepts, practices, and procedures within a particular field. Relies on instructions and pre-established guidelines to perform the functions of the job. Works under immediate supervision. Primary job functions do not typically require exercising independent judgment.

Essential Job Functions:

1. Prepares components of the cabinets to company standards to include deburring edges, peeling paper, cutting materials to prepare for assembly and welding.

3. Assembles cabinets completely and accurately in accordance with the print as evidenced by no damage to the doors, shelving, drawers, facings, slides, inner panels, hinges, locks and catches.

6. Processes job orders in a timely and accurate manner as evidenced by the completed traveler with appropriate job and item numbers.

7. Logs in timely to start the day and logs out at the end of the shift as well as on and off jobs accurately throughout the day on the E2 system as evidenced by the time records.

8. Demonstrates a motivated willingness to do the job and work at an appropriate pace and to produce a quality product as evidenced supervisors observation

9. Responsible to clean up area at the end of each shift as evidenced by supervisor’s observation.

10. Other duties as required by supervisor.

Minimum Requirements:

Requires a high school diploma or its equivalent. May be required to complete an apprenticeship and/or formal training in area of specialty. May require 0-2 years of experience in the field or in a related area.

Abilities Required:

1. Demonstrated ability to follow oral and written instructions.

2. Demonstrated knowledge of material, methods, tools and equipment.

3. Demonstrated ability to work in poor lighting, heating and ventilation.

4. Demonstrated ability to work in extreme hot and cold conditions.

5. Demonstrated ability to work in dirty and noisy areas.

6. Demonstrated ability to operate hand and power tools.

7. Demonstrated ability to interpret blueprints.

8. Demonstrated ability to sketch schematics.

9. Demonstrated ability to work in tight places.

10. Demonstrated ability to lift moderately heavy objects (50-90 pounds).

11. Demonstrated ability to do excessive walking, standing, bending and stooping.

12. Demonstrated ability to maintain proper attendance and punctuality standards.

title: Secondary Computing & Digital Subject Specialist
description:
Secondary Computing & Digital Subject Specialist

Salary: £45,000 - £50,000

STEM Learning has established a strong position in digital education through the National Centre for Computing Education (NCCE) and our wider work in computing, artificial intelligence and digital technologies. We are looking for an exceptional Computing & Digital Specialist to help drive our vision forward, bringing specialist expertise to shape high-quality professional learning, respond to emerging developments and influence the future of computing and digital education. Working across NCCE and wider STEM Learning programmes, you will play a key role in growing the reach, quality and impact of our offer and ensuring we continue to meet the evolving needs of teachers, education professionals and learners.

The Role

This role provides specialist expertise in secondary and post-16 computing and digital education across STEM Learning, contributing to the organisation’s strategic direction, programme development and wider educational impact. Working across the National Centre for Computing Education and other STEM Learning programmes, the role connects subject expertise, educational research, sector intelligence and emerging developments in technology to the design and delivery of high-quality professional learning.

The role contributes to the overall success of STEM Learning by ensuring that its computing and digital education provision is evidence-informed, innovative, responsive to curriculum and policy change, and aligned with the needs of education professionals and learners. Through collaboration with internal teams and external partners, the postholder will strengthen STEM Learning’s expertise, reach and influence, identify opportunities for growth and improvement, and help position the organisation as a leading voice in computing, artificial intelligence and digital education.

Our Ideal Candidate

Candidates will demonstrate our values: Sustainable – Innovative – Proactive

Qualifications/Skills/Experience/Competencies we are looking for include:

  • Significant professional experience in secondary and/or post-16 computing and digital education, with a strong understanding of curriculum, qualifications, pedagogy and current developments in the subject.
  • A relevant degree-level qualification or equivalent professional experience in computing, education or a related discipline.
  • Experience of designing, developing and delivering professional learning for teachers and/or other education professionals.
  • Experience of developing evidence-informed educational resources and professional learning, with the ability to translate research and evidence into effective practice.
  • Experience of building and managing effective partnerships with a range of stakeholders, including external organisations and delivery partners.
  • Experience of managing complex projects, competing priorities and deadlines, ideally within large-scale or national programmes.

Download the full Role Profile to find out more!

About Us

At STEM Learning, we work to improve lives through STEM education. We are a purpose-driven organisation, supporting teachers through high-impact professional development, inspiring young people to build confidence and curiosity in STEM, and connecting schools with employers to grow the UK’s future talent. Guided by our values, we focus our effort where it can make the greatest difference - helping all young people, whatever their background, to see themselves in STEM.

By joining us, you’ll:

Contribute to exciting, high-profile STEM initiatives that have a lasting impact on students and employers alike.

Work alongside passionate colleagues dedicated to shaping the future of STEM careers.

Be supported by a collaborative and dynamic work environment that fosters innovation and creativity.

Gain the opportunity to grow professionally.

Take a look inside the National STEM Learning Centre in York to see our facilities.

Our Benefits

  • 30 days holidays plus bank holidays
  • An additional day off on your birthday
  • Access to an attractive pension scheme
  • Our full-time hours are 37 hours per week
  • Up to 3 paid volunteering leave days per year
  • A comprehensive employee assistance programme

Next Steps

Closing date for applications: Friday 25th September 2026

Interview dates TBC

To Apply

Please provide us with:

  • Your up-to-date CV
  • A covering letter (no more than the equivalent of 2 sides of A4) explaining your interest in the role and why you think you would be the ideal candidate.

STEM Learning strives to be diverse and inclusive – a place where we can ALL be ourselves. We encourage applications from all backgrounds and communities, and are committed to employing teams with diverse abilities, skills, and experiences.

We foster a culture where every employee’s voice is respected and valued.

title: Psych Tech
description:
3 POSITIONS AVAILABLE IN GASTONIA (8P-8A, INCLUDES EVERY OTHER WEEKEND).

1 POSITION AVAILABLE IN SHELBY (8A-8P, INCLUDES EVERY OTHER WEEKEND).

General Position Description:

Under general supervision provides crisis support services to consumers receiving 24/7/365 crisis services. This may include the following levels of care/services; Gaylain’s House of Hope (for female staff as applicable) and/or any other service assigned by the supervisor. Primary duties include supporting the medical and clinical services being provided to consumers, including; maintaining a safe and therapeutic environment, assisting consumers with basic needs, e.g., providing bedding/towels, assisting with meal preparation, washing clothing, motivational counseling to enhance service delivery, transportation, and other duties assigned by supervisor.

Performance Expectations and Competencies

1. Shall demonstrate the use of knowledge/skill/judgment and provide 24/7/365 crisis management services that evidence ethical performance, and meet the needs of persons served and other stakeholders. Performance tasks shall include, but not be limited to:

a. Under the direct supervision of a supervisor or Team Lead RN, shall utilize knowledge/skill to maintain a safe and therapeutic environment and support professional services that are provided within 24/7/365 services.

b. Use of least restrictive interventions to promote consumer autonomy and assure safety for employees and other consumers on the unit.

c. Effective communication with consumers to enhance motivation and commitment to the recovery process.

d. Providing basic individual and group communication and support groups.

i. Daily Meditation

ii. WRAP Groups

iii. Orientation Groups

iv. Exercise

v. Basic Skill Development

vi. Social Activities

e. Taking accurate vital signs that include blood pressure, pulse, respirations monitoring general health status and safety, and observing self-administration or medication administration as applicable.

f. Consumer Documentation to include:

i. Understanding of rules and structure of the unit

ii. Self-medication and MAR forms.

g. Consumer Record Documentation to include:

i. Service Notes

ii. Confidentiality and Privacy Practice Documentation

iii. General admission and referral forms.

h. Transport of consumers to community resources.

i. Provide adequate supervision and adherence to the rules by the CTI consumers

j. Monitor and report to supervisor any issues that become apparent with a CTI consumer

k. Use of a community-based team approach that utilizes the resources of the community, consumer, and treatment team, to achieve positive consumer outcomes, stabilize the crisis, and appropriately transition the consumer to needed services and supports.

l. Shall demonstrate the ability to work/be a part of 24/7/365 organizational and therapeutic teams, and maintain positive working relationships with consumers, community stakeholders, referral organizations, and other employees/ departments of PCC.

m. Monitoring and maintaining internal control of consumer funds.

n. Shall develop a working knowledge of applicable organizational policy and procedure and demonstrate compliance. This shall include, but not be limited to:

· Personnel policies/procedures

· Employee Ethics/Corporate Compliance/Consumer Rights

(All Psych Techs/RSWs are required to complete upon hire and annually thereafter mandatory professional ethics training)

· Service record documentation

· Confidentiality/HIPAA

· Clinical Policy and Procedure

· Medication administration(as required by supervisor)

o. Shall complete other duties as assigned by supervisor.

General Knowledge and Skills Required for the Position:

General Knowledge of the dynamics of MH/DD/SA behavioral health disorders (BHD) and their impact upon persons served and their families; the bio/psycho/social factors involved in (BHD); up-to-date principles/techniques (evidence-based/best practices) of crisis response, prevention, and intervention application to individuals possessing (BHD); the community resources available to persons with (BHD), to include behavioral health, social service, community services, and self-help groups; knowledge of billing and service record documentation requirements, NC Division of MH/DD/SA, ASAM/MCO, CARF and PCC policy/procedure.

General Skill in the application of crisis assessment/prevention/intervention techniques that are considered ethical evidence-based/best practices as defined by the NC Division of MH/DD/SA, and/or literature/research, and organizational policy/procedure; skill in the delivery of services using accepted crisis treatment modalities, to include, individual, family, marital, and in-community; skill in establishing/maintaining effective therapeutic and professional relationships with persons served and/or their family members; behavioral health providers; and, skill in accurately documenting services provided and billed.

Preferred and Minimum Position Qualifications:

1. At a minimum, the individual must meet the NC Division of MH/DD/SA requirements for Paraprofessionals.

2. High School Diploma or equivalent.

3. At least one (1) year experience in delivering clinical crisis services. Credit may be given for previous crisis experience in other job positions, practicums, and internships as this experience relates to the provision of crisis services.

4. Preference may be given to individuals who are a Certified Peer Support Specialist (or pursuing certification) or Alcohol and Drug Counselor.

Additional Job Requirements (Licenses, Certifications, Personal Vehicle, etc.):

1. Valid driver’s license (may be waived by a supervisor if the individual is a certified peer support specialist or CSAC)

2. 24/7/365 shift work is required for this position which may include availability by phone to work shifts and cover increased acuity on the unit or as requested by the supervisor.

3. Must have the ability to lift to 20 pounds.

4. Must have the ability to move freely and be mobile for a minimum of 6 - 8 hours during work shift.

5. Travel is required as part of this position and may use the company-supplied vehicle and/or use of personal vehicle with mileage reimbursement as defined in PCC policy/procedure.

6. Must have the ability to operate a telephone, fax machine, and computer hardware/software.

7. Must have the ability to write in a manner that is legible/readable/understandable.

8. Willingness to work in a high-stress/risk environment that is driven by team performance

9. Transportation to and from work in various environmental conditions 24/7 services are essential services that must operate 24/7/365.

10. Must complete and remain in compliance with the following training/certifications:

a. First Aid/CPR

b. EBPI – A/B

c. Blood Borne Pathogens

d. Medication Management

e. Defensive Driving

f. Others as specified by program requirements.

Essential Equipment Routinely Used In This Position:

1. Computer and Software to include: Microsoft Office, Internet, and other database software

2. Telephone

3. Driving of automobile

4. Fax machine

5. Blood pressure, temperature equipment

title: Director, People Business Partner
description:
WHO WE ARE:

The National Multiple Sclerosis Society mobilizes people and resources to drive research for a cure and to address the challenges of everyone affected by MS. To fulfill this mission, the Society funds cutting-edge research, drives change through advocacy, facilitates professional education, collaborates with MS organizations around the world, and provides programs and services designed to help people with MS and their families move their lives forward. We partner with volunteers to accomplish our work. Staff members engage volunteers through effective and timely communications, facilitating meaningful opportunities, and continually seeking and providing feedback for reciprocal growth and learning.

Job Summary:

The Director, People Business Partner (People Business Partner Lead) is a key leader within the National MS Society (the Society) and, as such, must maintain a broad knowledge of our organization, exemplify our values, contribute positively to our mission, and collaborate in discussions and tactical project teams cross functionally.

The People Business Partner Lead aligns business objectives with employees and management across designated business units. The role is grounded in a deep understanding of the business and in trusted, credible relationships with leaders and employees, partnering across the People & Culture function to deliver value-added services that reflect the strategic objectives of the organization.

The People Business Partner Lead acts as a trusted advisor to business leaders, providing guidance on workforce planning, talent management, leadership development, employee relations, performance, organizational design, and culture while ensuring compliance with people policies and labor laws. It is essential that this individual serves as a knowledgeable and trusted business partner whose credibility is rooted in business acumen, fiscal stewardship, and alignment with our Mission, Vision, and Values - combined with deep HR expertise. Above all, this leader cares about people and acts as a strategic Business Partner Lead for assigned functions, providing thoughtful talent guidance and support with humility, humanity, and hospitality.

Location Requirements

  • Remote - Flexible Location

  • Prefence to those located near one of our hubs and/or within an hour of a major airport

  • ​Work is primarily performed remotely, however, when possible and necessary, teams meet in person to conduct the business of the organization and build team relationships.

  • Ability to travel approximately 20%

Compensation | Benefits:

The estimated hiring compensation range for this role is $90,000-$120,000. Final offers will be based on the candidate's geographic location, consider career experience, and may vary from this range due to these and other factors.

You will have the opportunity for a highly competitive, comprehensive benefit package that the Society provides to employees.

Your benefits include:

  • Considerable Paid Time Off Plan

  • Paid Holidays with a Winter Break

  • 401k Retirement Savings Plan with Society match

  • Commuter Benefit Plan

Comprehensive Health & Welfare benefits including:

  • Medical

  • Dental

  • Vision

  • Flex Spending Accounts

  • Life Insurance

  • Disability Coverage

  • Spring Health Membership offering free therapy and professional coaching, as well as additional voluntary benefit offerings.

Not to mention, you will join an incredible mission focused team of people!

Main Responsibilities:

  • Serve as the primary People Business Partner Lead supporting a function or group of functions throughout the entire employee lifecycle (EX: Development, Technology, or MarComms).

  • Partner with our People & Culture Lead and function leaders to co-create talent strategies that leverage best practices and are aligned with business and organizational goals.

  • Serve as an advisor and coach to our leaders (Talent Pipeline Portrait Levels: Leading Leaders, Leading Others, Knowledge Leaders and Knowledge Experts) enabling their leadership.

  • Build trusted relationships in 1:1 and group settings gaining knowledge and understanding in order to appropriately influence leadership decisions and drive organizational effectiveness.

  • Collaborate with our Recruiting team to proactively address current and future talent needs paying close attention to specialty skills and capabilities, budget constraints, title and pay parity, geographic needs, and longer-term succession planning.

  • Collaborate with functional leaders and Recruiting team to conduct internal assessments and external scans identifying talent gaps and considering how to address through internal interventions or through external acquisitions.

  • Use data and insights to build business cases for evolving talent strategies and practices.

  • Work jointly with business leaders to shape organizational design, define job roles, and optimize talent processes for performance and scalability.

  • Facilitate annual performance reviews, talent calibration, succession planning, and development conversations in partnership with leadership teams.

  • Ensure follow-through on development actions and readiness plans.

  • Collaborate with HR leadership to implement talent management initiatives (e.g., diversity and inclusion, succession planning) and deliver special projects on time and within scope.

  • Partner with stakeholders to distribute training materials on key HR topics such as workplace accommodation, and performance management.

  • Provide coaching, performance management, and development opportunities to direct reports within the Employee Relations and HR Admin function.

  • Lead and support the resolution of employee relations issues and investigations through effective partnership with the Business Partners, Legal, and Compliance teams, while providing tactical guidance to managers on complex employee matters to ensure regulatory compliance, mitigate risk, and promote positive employee outcomes and engagement.

  • Support execution of HR initiatives such as harassment training and ensure timely completion of administrative tasks including investigation documentation.

  • Coordinate onboarding and offboarding logistics with cross-functional teams (e.g., IT, HR shared services) and support exit interviews to ensure a smooth employee experience.

  • Contribute to ensuring employee records are accurately maintained in HR systems through coordinated efforts with HR operations teams.

  • Collaborate with legal, compliance, and HR teams to design, review, and update HR policies and procedures in line with legislation and best practices.

  • Partner with managers and employees to interpret and apply HR policies consistently, escalating complex issues as needed for resolution.

  • Advocate for client group requirements during the design and rollout of enterprise-wide HR programs to ensure relevance and adoption.

  • Lead change management efforts for talent-related initiatives, advising leaders on employee impact and deploying risk mitigation strategies to support successful transitions.

What We're Looking for:

  • Bachelor’s degree (or equivalent) in HR, Business, Industrial Relations, Organizational Development, or related field

  • Progressive leadership experience: 7+ years of experience in leadership roles, with a significant portion within Human Resources roles focused on Talent Management

  • Minimum of 7 years of progressive HR business partner experience with deep experience within the employee relations and conflict resolution space

  • Human resources or operations experience gained in the non-profit sector with peer to peer fundraising preferred

  • HR certification (e.g. CHRL, SHRP, PHR, SPHR) preferred

  • Strong communication skills honed through experience in various formats – verbal, written, remote, in person, 1;1, groups of all sizes, formal and informal, et cetera

  • Excellent EQ interpersonal skills, with the ability to partner effectively with people from all backgrounds and at various career stages and with a range of skills, education, and capabilities

  • Strong collaboration skills demonstrated within remote and hybrid teams

  • Capable as facilitator to engage, inspire, and communicate concepts and expectations

  • Experience creating best practices that leverage automation and AI to improve outcomes

  • Strong working knowledge and experience leveraging Workday HCM for HR business processes and workflows

  • Microsoft office suite: Proficient in Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Teams

  • Commitment to inclusion, diversity, equity, and accessibility (IDEA) principles

  • Ability to handle sensitive and confidential information with discretion

  • Analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to make data-driven decisions

  • Strong leadership and team management skills, with the ability to develop and mentor others in a REMOTE first environment

We’re committed to supporting the growth of every employee through a structured and transparent approach to career development. We use Talent Portraits to define clear expectations, development opportunities, and advancement paths — whether you're growing as a people leader or deepening your expertise as an individual contributor. Each role is thoughtfully placed within one of these pathways (Leadership or Partner) to help you understand how it fits into our broader organization and your potential career journey.

This position is classified as Knowledge Leader.

The National MS Society is committed to building a diverse and inclusive workforce. We strive to create a workforce that reflects the communities we serve and where everyone feels empowered to bring their authentic selves to work. We need you and your unique talents and perspectives to help us write the last chapter on MS.

APPLICATION INSTRUCTIONS:

We appreciate your consideration of our job opportunities and strive to make it as effortless as possible to apply for our positions. With only a few required sections and the option to use our resume parsing tool, we aim to streamline the application experience, saving you time and effort. We appreciate your interest in joining our team and look forward to receiving your application!

title: Small Group Training Instructor
description:
Job Title: Small Group Training Instructor

Job Purpose

The Small Group Training Instructor is responsible for leading safe, engaging, and motivating small group training sessions. This role delivers high-quality coaching, provides personalized attention within a group setting, and supports members in achieving their fitness goals while upholding the facility’s standards for service, safety, and professionalism.

Operations

Program Delivery

  • Plan, prepare, and deliver structured small group training sessions aligned with facility guidelines and training philosophies.
  • Demonstrate correct exercise techniques and ensure proper form for all participants.
  • Modify exercises for varying fitness levels, limitations, and goals.
  • Maintain high energy, engagement, and motivation throughout each session.

Member Experience

  • Build rapport with participants and create a welcoming, inclusive training environment.
  • Provide individual coaching cues, support, and accountability within a group model.
  • Track participant progress when required and offer feedback to help members improve performance and achieve goals.
  • Communicate clearly and professionally with participants before, during, and after sessions.

Safety & Professional Standards

  • Ensure all sessions follow facility safety standards and industry best practices.
  • Properly inspect equipment before and after sessions; report maintenance needs promptly.
  • Maintain required certifications, including CPR/AED.
  • Adhere to all organizational policies, procedures, and customer service expectations.

Team Collaboration

  • Attend staff meetings, trainings, and continuing education sessions as required.
  • Collaborate with the fitness team to support programming, special events, and member engagement initiatives.
  • Assist in promoting small group training programs within the facility.

Requirements

  • Current nationally recognized fitness certification (e.g., NASM, ACE, ISSA, ACSM, AFAA, NFPT).
  • Current CPR/AED certification.
  • Experience coaching individuals or groups in a fitness environment.
  • Strong communication and motivational skills.

Preferred

  • Previous experience specifically with small group training formats (functional training, HIIT, strength circuits, etc.).
  • Knowledge of corrective exercise or functional movement training.
  • Ability to work varied hours—including early mornings, evenings, or weekends as needed.

Physical Requirements

  • Ability to demonstrate exercises and perform physical movements for extended periods.
  • Ability to lift and move equipment up to 50 pounds.
  • Ability to monitor participants visually and verbally to ensure safety.

Core Competencies

  • Coaching & Instruction
  • Member Engagement
  • Safety Awareness
  • Professionalism
  • Teamwork
  • Adaptability
  • Leadership

  • kiinnostusta laadukkaan lounasruoan valmistamiseen

  • Responsible for reviewing and submitting NIBRS (National Incident Based Reporting System) data to the Colorado Bureau of Investigation (CBI) and FBI, complying with State and Federal requirements and responsible for quality assurance of NIBRS entry and reporting.

Interviews and obtains/manages the personal information/data on each sex offender to ensure compliance with CBI policy to ensure the agency meets the state compliance requirements. Uses CCIC/NCIC terminal to enter/validate any outstanding warrants, or changes to offender's records, and uses COSOR to enter offender registrations. Responds to callers, other inquiries from law enforcement, probation, and parole as needed.
  • Acts as Civil Process Clerk - Receives, prepares, processes, and records time mandated court and legal documents for service of process according to Colorado law. Tracks billing process.
  • Processes and maintains Concealed Handgun Permit (CHP) applications which includes fingerprint supported background checks. Researches various databases and resources, and obtains confidential CCIC/NCIC background information to assist the Sheriff in issuance/denial/revocation of permits.
  • Acts as Accounts Payable Clerk - Responds to external vendors and internal managers regarding all aspects of the accounts payable process. Processes invoices for payment for all departments in accordance with county practices, Verifies the accuracy of vendor invoices and confirm that the correct general ledger account codes are used. Produces annual, monthly, and weekly reports for administrative staff.
  • Prepares deposits for all incoming financial transactions in accordance with county policy.
  • Utilizes a variety of secure and confidential law enforcement and court computer systems to perform duties of this position.
  • Maintains knowledge of Sheriff’s office operations in order to assist all customers, including, but not limited to: greeting and determining customers’ needs; providing accurate information or services specific to the Sheriff’s office; and/or referring to appropriate person/ services. Answers, screens and transfers calls in a positive, professional, and knowledgeable manner. Takes accurate messages. Assists with making/returning phone calls as necessary.
  • Prepares correspondence, reports, forms, documents from drafts, notes, corrected copy, or prior materials using a computer with form templates.
  • Establishes and maintains office files, follows an established filing system; compiles information from such files; purges files as required.
  • Operates standard office equipment, including job related computer hardware and software applications for data entry, facsimile equipment and multi-line telephones, may operate a two-way radio or other department specific equipment.
  • Performs related duties and responsibilities as required.
  • Collects fees from public and utilizes the cash register according to county guidelines.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.
  • Provides training and guidance to newly hired employees in this position to ensure successful on-boarding and adherence to departmental standards.

Additional Duties:

  • Issues dog tags and maintains dog tag database.
  • Makes copies and faxes documents.
  • Updates office supply inventory and notifies Administrative Manager of items to be ordered
  • Sorts, distributes, and processes incoming and outgoing mail, including legal and time sensitive correspondence, for administration, patrol, detentions, dispatch, and victim services. May drive to other County buildings and Post Office to process mail and relay.

Flexibility is essential to accommodate community events outside of standard business hours.

This is a community-based position, and candidates must reside in New Hanover or Brunswick County. You must be comfortable traveling to the following counties:

Management preference: Experience with the unhomed population and/or community-based experience.

How You'll Benefit:
Being part of our team means we value and encourage your personal growth and development. You'll earn an hourly rate of $18; we offer competitive benefits to benefits eligible positions.

Our Benefits Include:
  • Time Off: PTO to recharge and relax.
  • Comprehensive Benefits: Medical, dental, and vision coverage, plus an optional Flexible Spending Account (FSA).
  • Mileage: Mileage reimbursement in addition to your hourly pay.
  • Financial Security: Life and disability insurance, along with a 403(b)-retirement plan.
  • Loan Relief: Public Student Loan Forgiveness qualifier.
  • Support Services: Access to our Employee Assistance Program and legal services when you need them.

What We're Looking For:
To join our team as the Education and Outreach Specialist you must have working relationships with community referrals, the ability to manage multiple projects, and have great attention to detail. We also require the following:
  • High School diploma or GED required.
  • Maintain valid NC driver's license and auto insurance for personal and agency vehicles utilized for work.

If you're a kind, enthusiastic person seeking a rewarding opportunity where you can make a huge difference in the daily lives of the people you will help, please visit

About Easterseals PORT Health:
Easterseals PORT Health is a trustworthy, compassionate partner providing exceptional disability, behavioral health and addiction treatment services to help our neighbors live their best lives. Our diverse and inclusive 2,600-member team provides meaningful support to 40,200 kids, adults and families in 11,000 home, facility and community locations across North Carolina and Virginia.

Our working environment supports employee and client health with a 'no tobacco' use policy (tobacco free and smoke free) in all offices, client facilities, properties, and agency vehicles.

We believe that by leveraging the unique strengths and perspectives of our workforce, we can advance our just cause, while building a healthy, sustainable organization. That's why we listen, seek to understand & act to make ESPH an Inclusive Culture, Different Voices, Embracing Potential, Authentic Self & Learning & Growing (IDEAL) organization.

Applicants of all abilities are encouraged to apply!

title: Executive Personal Assisant
description:
At Platinum Fundraising, you’ll have the opportunity to make a real difference while building a rewarding career supporting the Founder of the Company. Being in business for over 25 years, we are helping schools, youth athletic organizations, and non-profits raise millions of dollars through our proven fundraising programs that empower kids and strengthen communities!

Platinum Fundraising is seeking an exceptional Executive & Personal Assistant to serve as a trusted right-hand to one of our company owners. This is not a traditional administrative role, as we need someone who sees what needs to happen next, takes ownership, and keeps things moving. The successful candidate will be comfortable managing a broad mix of professional and personal priorities and can be trusted to handle matters from start to finish with sound judgment, discretion, and excellent follow-through.

Key Responsibilities

  • Manage the executive’s calendar, appointments, meetings, and changing priorities.
  • Coordinate business and personal travel, including flights, transportation, reservations, and itineraries; proactively manage delays, cancellations, and other disruptions.
  • Track projects, deadlines, outstanding items, commitments, and items assigned to others; follow through until completion.
  • Prepare for meetings, take notes as needed, and track action items.
  • Coordinate smaller projects, vendors, quotes, services, meetings, events, gifts, supplies, and special projects.
  • Track receipts and expenses; maintain highly organized electronic and physical files.
  • Prepare franchisee packages; review franchisee documents and Fundraising Specialist contracts for accuracy and completeness.
  • Maintain CRM/VanillaSoft updates, lead status changes, franchisee records, files, and reports.
  • Review form submissions, coverage maps, and location information; support territory and store-location administration.
  • Track franchisee-provided leads, monitor new territory activity, follow up on customer survey responses, and draft/respond to Google reviews.
  • Manage personal appointments, personal travel, purchases, gifts, returns, household vendors, paperwork, phone inquiries, and occasional local errands.
  • Handle confidential business and personal information with complete discretion.

What Success Looks Like

You naturally stay a step ahead. You anticipate needs, recognize potential issues early, and take initiative to keep things moving without waiting for direction.

When something changes or goes wrong, you assess the situation, consider what may be affected, and take ownership of finding a solution. You follow through, stay on top of outstanding items, adapt when priorities change, and make sure important details do not fall through the cracks.

Success in this role means becoming a trusted right-hand. Someone who can be given something and relied upon to manage it thoughtfully from start to finish, with confidence that it is handled.

Qualifications & Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree required.
  • 5+ years of relevant Executive Assistant and/or Personal Assistant experience.
  • Experience in a combined Executive + Personal Assistant role strongly preferred.
  • Experience directly supporting an owner, founder, or senior executive.
  • Experience managing a busy executive calendar, coordinating business travel, and supporting projects.
  • Demonstrated ability to handle highly confidential information; NDA required.
  • Very tech-savvy with the ability to learn and troubleshoot systems independently; strong proficiency with Microsoft Office and PDF tools.

Compensation

$75k - $95k, based upon experience.

Benefits

  • Medical, Vision, and Dental Insurance with company contribution
  • Paid Time Off
  • Paid Holidays
  • Health Savings Account (HSA)
  • Flexible Spending Account (FSA)
  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
  • Paid Training
  • Employee Rewards
  • Employee Discounts
  • Veteran Appreciation Floating Holiday
  • Annual salary review

Perks

We take pride in creating a comfortable, well-equipped workspace where every team member can stay focused, energized, and supported throughout the day.

  • No cold prospecting. We provide all the leads for our specialists!
  • We believe highly in work-life balance so only 40-hour work weeks and No Weekends!
  • Extensive and Paid Training Program that will set you up for success in the role!
  • Enjoy a relaxed dress code that lets you focus on performance, not wardrobe. From jeans and sneakers to comfortable sweats, we want you feeling your best to perform at your best.
  • We believe great energy starts with great snacks, from coffee and tea to bagels, fruit, and a candy jar that never disappoints. Help yourself to our complimentary office treats and keep the good vibes going all day!
  • Enjoy complimentary coffee or tea to start your day, snacks, and fresh fruit in the office.
  • Recharge in style with our luxury massage chair and ultra-comfortable LoveSacs, the perfect way to unwind between calls.
  • Choose your comfort from ergonomic office chairs to balance ball chairs that keep you moving and energized throughout the day.
  • Work to the soundtrack of good vibes. Our state-of-the-art sound system keeps the office filled with your favorite hits, old and new.

Culture

We celebrate everything — every sale, every milestone, every personal win, because we believe in recognizing effort as much as results. At Platinum Fundraising, you’ll join a team that lifts each other up, learns together, and pushes each other to be better every day.

Our leaders are hands-on, offering constant coaching and guidance to help you succeed and close more deals. Add in great incentives, friendly competition, and a fun, inclusive environment, and you’ve got a place where you can thrive both personally and professionally.

Want to see our team in action? Check us out! :

Schedule & Logistics

This is a full-time, fully in-office position in Fort Lauderdale.

Schedule is Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM. Hours may vary based on business needs. Occasional availability outside normal business hours and occasional travel may be required.

Candidates must have a valid driver’s license, reliable transportation, and be comfortable completing occasional local errands.

The Right Fit

This role is best suited for someone who genuinely enjoys being the person behind the scenes who makes everything run smoothly. You take pride in anticipating needs, solving problems, and making sure nothing falls through the cracks. For the right person, this is an opportunity to become a highly trusted partner and true right-hand to a company owner.

title: Municipal Court Juvenile Clerk
description:
SUMMARY

Performs specialized clerical and administrative duties for the Bedford Municipal Court, with primary responsibility for the processing, scheduling, documentation, and monitoring of juvenile cases. Maintains accurate and confidential court records; assists defendants, parents, guardians, and the public in person, by telephone, and through written and electronic correspondence; and ensures compliance with applicable court orders, state and local laws, and City policies. Coordinates juvenile case compliance, sanctions, diversion programs, community service, and related court activities, and serves as a liaison between the Municipal Court, families, schools, community organizations, Teen Court, other courts, and state agencies.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

1. Schedules and prepares juvenile cases for court proceedings and maintains accurate, complete, and current juvenile case files and records. Coordinates juvenile docket schedules with the Municipal Court Manager and Municipal Court Judge and prepares, organizes, and verifies dockets and supporting case documentation prior to court.

2. Serves as the primary staff member responsible for inbound telephone calls and provides secondary coverage at the court service window. Provides professional assistance to defendants, parents, guardians, and the public regarding court procedures, citations, court dates, payment arrangements, and available options.

3. Performs computer data entry, import, and verification of juvenile and adult citations and other Class C misdemeanor charges filed in Municipal Court. Ensures the accuracy of case information and completes all required processing in the Municipal Court software. Processes driver’s license checks through the State of Texas database and verifies information for accuracy.

4. Records case dispositions, court orders, payment arrangements, and other case activity in the Municipal Court. Collects authorized court fines and fees and accurately records amounts collected and payment arrangements when working at the court service window.

5. Provides defendants with information regarding available options, court procedures, and applicable rights concerning their citations within the scope of authorized duties. Assists defendants, parents, guardians, and the public in person, by telephone, and through mail and email.

6. Monitors compliance with court orders and takes appropriate action when non-compliance occurs. Processes applicable sanctions and notices, including DIC-81, DIC-15, and Juvenile Now Adult notices, and files required documentation with the State of Texas.

7. Coordinates juvenile court docket schedules and related case preparation with the Municipal Court Manager and Municipal Court Judge.

8. Monitors compliance with deferred sentences and other court-ordered requirements for juvenile defendants. Works with the Municipal Court Judge regarding non-compliance in Alcoholic Beverage Code cases. Reports non-compliant Teen Court and Juvenile Diversion cases and coordinates Show Cause Hearings as directed.

9. Ensures juvenile case information and contact information remain current. Notifies juvenile defendants, parents, or guardians of violations, court orders, and pending court dates as required.

10. Coordinates court-ordered community service for juvenile and adult defendants, including scheduling, documentation, and monitoring of completion. Maintains and updates the list of approved nonprofit community service organizations. Prepares community service orientation packets for juvenile and adult defendants. Maintains and updates lists of approved Alcohol, Tobacco, and Drug education classes and other court-ordered programs. Coordinates community service activities involving the Municipal Court.

11. Acts as a liaison between the Municipal Court and parents, guardians, schools, community service organizations, Teen Court, county courts, and state agencies. Serves as the primary division contact for matters involving the juvenile caseload and coordinates information and documentation with appropriate internal and external agencies.

12. Processes weekly delinquent citations and provides required notifications to defendants by mail.

13. Scans and electronically files juvenile and adult documents, court forms, correspondence, and closed case documents into the Municipal Court software.

14. Performs other related duties, assignments, and special projects as required.

15. Maintains regular and timely attendance and conducts all interactions with coworkers, defendants, families, and the public in a professional, courteous, and respectful manner.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

This job has no supervisory responsibilities.

QUALIFICATIONS -To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

EDUCATION and/or EXPERIENCE

High school diploma / GED, plus two years related Municipal Court, legal, or records experience and/or training with one year experience as a cashier/teller; or equivalent combination of education and experience.

LANGUAGE SKILLS

Ability to read and comprehend simple instructions, short correspondence, and memos. Ability to write simple correspondence. Ability to effectively present information in one-on-one and in small group situations to defendants, citizens, and other employees of the organization.

MATHEMATICAL SKILLS

Ability to add and subtract two-digit numbers and to multiply and divide with 10's and 100's. Ability to perform these operations using units of American money and weight measurement, volume, and distance.

REASONING ABILITY

Ability to apply common sense understanding to carry out instructions furnished in written, oral, or diagram form. Ability to deal with problems involving several concrete variables in standardized situations.

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

  • Must possess a valid Texas Driver’s License.
  • Must be bondable.
  • Must possess, or have the ability to obtain, Texas Municipal Court Clerk Certification Level 1 within twenty-four (24) months of hire.
  • Must successfully complete a Criminal Justice Information Services (CJIS) fingerprint-based background check and maintain eligibility for CJIS access. Due to CJIS requirements related to access to criminal justice information, disqualifying factors may include felony convictions, felony deferred adjudication, Class A or Class B misdemeanor deferred adjudication, Class B misdemeanor convictions, an open arrest for any criminal offense (felony or misdemeanor), and convictions involving family violence.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Current Texas Municipal Court Clerk Certification Level 1.
  • Membership in the Texas Court Clerks Association.
  • Fluency in Spanish.

SPECIALIZED KSA'S

· Must have demonstrated knowledge of use and application of computer software relevant to the position. Must have working knowledge of and be familiar with modern office equipment.

· Must have demonstrated skill to operate a 10-key calculator by touch.

· Must have strong organizational skills.

· Keyboarding/typing skills.

· Must be able to work effectively individually as well as within a team environment.

· Must be able to maintain mental focus during work activities.

.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to talk or hear. The employee frequently is required to stand; walk; sit; use hands to finger, handle, or feel; and reach with hands and arms. The employee is occasionally required to climb or balance and stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl. The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 25 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus.

WORK ENVIRONMENT

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is occasionally exposed to moving mechanical parts and high, precarious places. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate.

EDUCATION and/or EXPERIENCE

High school diploma / GED, plus two years related Municipal Court, legal, or records experience and/or training with one year experience as a cashier/teller; or equivalent combination of education and experience.

title: Team Leader
description:
In Tampa, our Team Jeni's Team Leaders have the opportunity to earn an average of $24.50 per hour!*

*This is an estimate of hourly earnings. It is based on the 2026 base pay rate, plus 2025's hourly tip average. 2026 actual customer tips may vary.

In Florida, if the average hourly earnings of a Team Leader are less than $17 per hour in a two-week pay period, Jeni's will add the difference to the person’s paycheck so that their average hourly earnings reach $17 per hour for that pay period.

Jeni’s Splendid Ice Creams is searching for part-time Team Leaders to join our Pearl team.

At Jeni’s, we’re devoted to making better ice creams and bringing people together. Our scoop shops are at the heart of how we serve this mission. They are where we offer the ice creams we work so hard to build from the ground up—where people come together to share joy and conversation. We love people. We love ice cream. We view ice cream as a form of art.

Team Jeni’s Team Leaders are part-time crew members who lead shifts. In addition to leading shifts, they scoop and serve ice cream to our customers, make waffle products, run the register with cash management responsibilities, keep the shop clean, change out buckets of ice cream, and perform a number of other important, related tasks.

As a Team Leader, you will:

  • Serve the ice cream Time magazine calls “the best in America”

  • Gain valuable real-world business and entrepreneurship experience

  • Work in an environment oriented around serving each other and making people’s day

  • Lead shifts and act as a role model for other team members

  • Have opportunities for growth within a growing company

  • Receive competitive compensation

Qualities of Team Leaders:

  • Exhibit passion for community, an eye for detail, a willingness to clean (a lot), stamina (to serve people in long lines), and the ability to work in a fast-paced environment

  • The ability to positively influence and lead a shift of ambassadors, helping them uphold the highest standards and feel supported

  • Resourceful and calm when challenges come up

  • Have great judgment, common sense, and be skillful interpersonally

  • Familiar with (and be able to articulate to customers) what distinguishes Jeni’s Splendid Ice Creams from other ice creams, and be able to articulate that to the 500th customer with the same care and presence as the 1st customer

  • Available to work weekends, late nights (past 11 p.m.)

  • Provide consistent, world-class service to every single customer

  • Reliable, on time, and ready to hustle for every shift

  • Committed to the well-being of their shop team, their community, and the environment around them

About Jeni’s Splendid Ice Creams:

Founded by Jeni Britton in 2002, Jeni's Splendid Ice Creams is a B Corp headquartered in Columbus, Ohio, with scoop shops in over twenty cities across the country, making it possible for members of Team Jeni’s who are interested in developing their careers, or transitioning to a new city, to have meaningful opportunities to learn, grow, and explore.

Our Team Leaders make a difference in their shop, their community, and in how they partner with their team and serve their customers. If this opportunity sounds delicious to you, please apply.

Jeni's is an equal opportunity employer. Said our way, we love and honor differences, and we love sharing common values such as talent, hustle, guts, resilience, and empathy. Our differences are a primary source of our team's strength and we crave having a team rich with diversity which is creativity and art in its human form.

title: Day Program Coordinator
description:
The Day Program Coordinator is responsible for supervising Day Program Staff in carrying out the Individualized Day Program Plans of iCare members with developmental disabilities and serious behavioral issues. The Day Program Coordinator will work with the day program staff to ensure that the members receive the individualized prescribed programming in a community setting that supports the personal needs and goals of their plans.


Responsibilities


Under the direction of the Manager of Program Services, the Day Program Coordinator is responsible for the following:

  • Day-to-day supervision and training of Day Program Staff in strategies for development of each assigned member’s behavioral, communication, and skill goals. This requires a thorough knowledge of each member’s Individualized Day Program Plan, and the ability to teach and communicate effectively with Day Program Staff.
  • Apply for potential members in DDD Focus system daily.
  • Assist in conducting facility tours/program to potential members/parent/guardians.
  • Providing monthly one hour training to Day Program Staff in a group setting on such topics as data collection, scheduling, supportive relationships, basic care, and behavioral interventions. This includes coordinating plans with Program Managers in the hour before the meeting.
  • Ensure staff worked hours are verified and input into the system correctly to be signed.
  • Publishing and distributing a Day Program Activities Calendar on a monthly basis that is designed for teaching community integration skills and providing social and recreational opportunities. Requires sending daily text messages/email to all Day Program Staff to coordinate group activities.
  • Ensuring that the members are transported to and participate in these activities with full involvement from the Day Program Staff who are responsible for each individual member’s care. The Day Program Coordinator is expected to be an active participant at all calendared group events.
  • Teaching art, exercise, or music classes as needed and supporting Day Program Staff in preparing and presenting activities. Organizing special events such as holiday celebrations, including decorating the party room, coordinating food, games, and dance music.
  • Reviewing the members’ daily program notes taken by Day Program Staff. Tallying behavioral and skill goal data into a specified format and writing a narrative overview and analysis of the data for each member’s quarterly day program report. Updating individual weekly schedules as the need arises.
  • Purchasing of supplies for day program activities including food for the cooking class, art supplies, and sports gear within a budgeted allowance for general program expenses.
  • Scheduling coverage for Day Program Staff’ vacations, sick time, and other time off in collaboration with Program Managers. In the event that staff coverage is not available, the Day Program Coordinator will step in and provide temporary care and supervision to the members and follow the members’ usual schedule.

Supervision

The Day Program Manager/Director is the direct supervisor of the Day Program Coordinator. The Day Program Coordinator will also be expected to work cooperatively with the Program Managers of the iCare facilities in which the members reside.

Job Requirements

  • Attendance at monthly staff and day program meetings.
  • Attendance at iCare In-Service Trainings. Must meet regulatory requirement of 12 hours of training per year.
  • As a mandated abuse reporter, the Day Program Coordinator must have the ability to recognize the obvious and suspected signs of abuse and is responsible for understanding and following abuse reporting policies and procedures.

Qualifications

  • Must be at least age 21.
  • Minimum of three years’ direct support experience in programs for the developmentally disabled, including supervisory experience.
  • Must have First Aid, CPR, Prevention & Support, Article 9, Medication Administration (if required).
  • Good written and verbal communication skills.
  • In addition, a clean driving record, with insurance company approval to operate iCare vehicles, is required.

title: Scrum Master (Remote Opportunity)
description:

The ideal candidate will be responsible for guiding and facilitating Agile practices within the team, ensuring smooth project execution, and helping the team meet its goals.

  • Build strong relationships to foster collaboration, transparency, and innovation across highly cross-functional Agile software development teams supporting CI/CD.

  • Champion Agile values and quality practices, coordinate across organizations, and coach team members on process improvements and best practices.
  • Work closely with senior-level client leadership and business stakeholders, advising on process standardization and continuous improvement.
  • Guide the development team in self-organization, cross-functionality, and adopting Agile principles to maximize performance.

  • Minimum of 5 years of professional experience.
  • Proven track record managing large-scale software development, data management, and system integration initiatives.

  • Proficient with Agile project management tools such as Jira, Trello, or similar platforms.
  • Familiarity with the Scaled Agile Framework (SAFe) and Kanban methodologies is highly desired.

Additional Qualifications:

  • Experience with SAFe/Agile.
  • Certified SAFe/Agile/Scrum certifications are preferred.
  • Experience with the VA or other Government agencies.
  • Ability to obtain government clearance.

Benefits:

  • Medical/Dental/Vision
  • PTO + Federal Holidays
  • Corporate Laptop
  • Training opportunities
  • 401(k) with employer match
  • Remote work options

Note: Selected candidates will be required to complete fingerprinting at a government facility and undergo a background check as part of the hiring process.

Mind Computing is an equal opportunity employer. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, or protected veteran status.

At this time, we are unable to offer sponsorship.

title: Data & AI Product Manager
description:
Description

The Data & AI Product Manager, Digital will lead the strategy, development, and evolution of enterprise data, analytics, and AI products that enable faster, more consistent, and forward-looking business decision-making across the organization.

This role will help build foresight capabilities, enterprise insights infrastructure, advanced analytics capabilities, and scalable learning systems that future-proof how the organization understands market performance, consumers, and business opportunities.

A key focus will be transforming complex and fragmented market performance data into scalable, AI-powered business intelligence capabilities—moving beyond traditional reporting toward automated insights, conversational analytics, intelligent data harmonization, and decision-support experiences.

The role will operate at the intersection of business strategy, data, analytics, AI, engineering, and user experience, owning products from strategy and discovery through launch, adoption, optimization, and lifecycle management.

Descriptiobn Continued

Data & AI Product Strategy

  • Own the multi-year product vision, strategy, roadmap, and prioritization for strategic enterprise data, analytics, and AI products.
  • Translate enterprise and Digital priorities into scalable product capabilities that improve how leaders and teams access insights and make decisions.
  • Identify opportunities to evolve traditional reporting and analytics into AI-powered intelligence and decision-support products.

End-to-End Product Ownership

  • Own the full product lifecycle across discovery, requirements, design, development, testing, launch, adoption, optimization, and transition/decommissioning.
  • Translate business needs into clear product requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, and prioritized product backlogs.
  • Make product trade-offs across business value, user experience, technical feasibility, scalability, cost, and time-to-value.
  • Partner with engineering and architecture teams to ensure solutions are reliable, scalable, maintainable, and aligned with enterprise technology standards.

AI-Powered Insights & Foresight

  • Drive the evolution of product capabilities including AI-enabled experiences, conversational analytics, automated insight generation, anomaly and opportunity detection, intelligent harmonization, and decision support.
  • Partner with Data Science, AI, Engineering, and business teams to identify high-value AI use cases and translate them into scalable product capabilities.
  • Establish appropriate human-in-the-loop workflows, transparency, validation, and monitoring for AI-generated insights.
  • Continuously evaluate emerging data and AI capabilities and determine where they can create meaningful business value.

Business Partnership & Cross-Functional Product Delivery

  • Create alignment around product vision, priorities, scope, success measures, and roadmap.
  • Serve as the bridge between business users and technical teams, ensuring products solve meaningful business problems rather than simply deliver technical functionality.
  • Orchestrate delivery across Product, Data Engineering, Analytics, Data Science/AI, Architecture, UX, business teams, governance functions, and strategic vendors.
  • Establish clear ownership, decision rights, dependencies, milestones, and escalation paths across complex enterprise initiatives.
  • Manage strategic vendors and partners where required while maintaining clear internal ownership of product strategy and outcomes.

Adoption, Value & Product Performance

  • Define product success measures spanning adoption, engagement, data quality, reliability, efficiency, user experience, decision impact, and measurable business value.
  • Drive adoption through stakeholder engagement, enablement, change management, documentation, and continuous product improvement.
  • Ensure product investments are connected to measurable business outcomes rather than delivery milestones alone.

Qualifications

  • 6+ years of experience across data/analytics product management, digital product management, analytics, data strategy, or related roles, including experience owning complex enterprise products.
  • 3+ years of direct product management experience preferred, including responsibility for product strategy, roadmap, prioritization, requirements, delivery, and adoption.
  • Demonstrated experience building or managing enterprise data, analytics, business intelligence, or AI-enabled products.
  • Strong understanding of modern data and analytics ecosystems, including SQL, cloud data platforms, data pipelines, semantic/data models, APIs, BI platforms, and AI/ML capabilities.
  • Technical familiarity with GCP, Databricks, SQL, and Python strongly preferred.
  • Experience with Looker, Power BI, or comparable business intelligence and analytics platforms preferred.
  • Experience with GenAI, conversational analytics, AI agents, automated insights, or AI-enabled enterprise products strongly preferred.
  • Strong understanding of data quality, governance, metadata, security, privacy, and responsible AI considerations within enterprise environments.
  • Demonstrated ability to translate ambiguous business problems and executive decision needs into clear product strategies and scalable technical capabilities.
  • Strong product judgment with the ability to prioritize across competing business needs, technical constraints, user experience, and long-term scalability.
  • Experience operating across global, cross-functional, and highly matrixed organizations.
  • Strong stakeholder management and executive communication skills, with the ability to influence without direct authority.
  • Highly analytical and comfortable defining and using product metrics to evaluate adoption, performance, and business value.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to communicate effectively across business, technical, and executive audiences.
  • Collaborative, curious, resourceful, and comfortable operating in an evolving environment where not all requirements or solutions are known upfront.

title: Department Clerk I, Senior Care PACE
description:
We are so glad you are interested in joining Sutter Health!

Organization:
