title: Managing Director
description:
Ideals Today BV, a PCS Wireless company, operates a direct-to-consumer business focused on mobile accessories and related products. We are seeking a Managing Director to take overall responsibility for the performance and operations of the business.

The Managing Director will have end-to-end accountability for Ideals Today BV, including commercial performance, operations, financial results, customer experience, and oversight of the third-party service provider supporting the business. This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who can drive growth, improve performance, and ensure strong execution across the organization.

Job Responsibilities:

· Own the overall strategy, P&L, performance, and day-to-day oversight of Ideals Today BV.

· Develop and execute plans to drive revenue growth, profitability, and sustainable business performance.

· Oversee key business areas, including e-commerce, operations, inventory, fulfillment, customer experience, and financial performance.

· Manage the third-party service provider, establishing clear expectations, KPIs, service levels, and accountability.

· Monitor financial, commercial, and operational performance and take action to address gaps and opportunities.

· Evaluate pricing, product assortment, promotions, customer trends, and market opportunities.

· Drive improvements in customer experience, operational efficiency, processes, and cost management.

· Partner with PCS Wireless leadership and functional teams to ensure alignment with broader business priorities.

· Manage key vendors and external partners and ensure appropriate business controls and regulatory compliance.

· Identify business risks and opportunities and provide clear recommendations to PCS Wireless leadership.

Who You Are:

· Experienced business leader with responsibility for a business, business unit, or significant commercial operation.

· Experience in direct-to-consumer, e-commerce, retail, consumer electronics, mobile accessories, or a related industry.

· Strong P&L management, financial, and commercial acumen.

· Experience overseeing multiple business functions and managing third-party service providers or outsourced operations.

· Strong understanding of e-commerce, including pricing, inventory, fulfillment, and customer experience.

· Data-driven, commercially minded, and comfortable making decisions in a fast-moving environment.

· Strong leadership, problem-solving, negotiation, and relationship-management skills.

· Experience operating within European markets; excellent English communication skills, with additional European languages an advantage.

We Are Seeking People Who:

title: County Planner
description:
Organization

Highway Engineering & Development Services

Pay

$9,024.03

Pay Frequency

Monthly

Full Time / Part Time

Full time

Job Summary

Under administrative direction, plans, organizes, directs, and oversees all operations, staff, and programs of the Development Services Department. The Director provides strategic leadership and management for planning, permitting and inspections; establishes departmental goals, policies, and budgets; and represents the department before elected officials, member communities, partner agencies, and the public.

Job Description

Safety-Sensitive Position: Yes (as defined under Oklahoma Statute Title 63 § 427.8)

All candidates conditionally offered transfer, promotion or initial hiring into a DOT/safety-sensitive position shall submit to testing for drugs and alcohol and test negative before performing any job functions that are safety-sensitive or require a CDL. External job applicants with a confirmed positive drug or alcohol test results shall be denied employment and shall be required to wait one year before applying for another position within Tulsa County.

Essential Job Functions

  • Plan, organize, direct, and evaluate the overall operations, programs, and services of the Planning and Development Services Department.
  • Prepare planning documents, reports, and recommendations for Tulsa County Planning Commission and Tulsa County Board of Adjustment.
  • Assist municipalities with plan updates and new plan development to ensure alignment with County goals.
  • Provide leadership and direction to departmental staff, including the Planning Division, Permitting Division and Planning Division; establish performance expectations and evaluate results.
  • Interpret and ensure compliance with the county building codes, electrical codes, plumbing codes, mechanical codes, sign codes and zoning codes.
  • Develop, recommend, and implement departmental goals, objectives, policies, procedures, and long-range plans consistent with the organization's mission.
  • Prepare, administer, and monitor the department budget; allocate resources, control expenditures, and recommend staffing levels.
  • Oversee the preparation and review of planning studies, comprehensive and area plans, zoning and land-use recommendations, and development applications.
  • Represent the department before boards, commissions, elected officials, member communities, partner agencies, and the public; present reports and recommendations.
  • Coordinate interdepartmental and intergovernmental projects, grants, and partnerships.
  • Ensure departmental compliance with applicable federal, state, and local laws, regulations, and professional standards.
  • Resolve complex and sensitive operational, personnel, and stakeholder issues.
  • Respond to public and developer inquiries related to planning, zoning, permits, and County regulations, providing clear guidance within established authority.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Additional Job Description

Qualifications Required

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential job function satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and abilities required. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Required Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

Knowledge of the principles and practices of urban and regional planning, land use, zoning, and development services; GIS principles and applications and of public administration, budgeting, and personnel management; applicable federal, state, and local laws, regulations, and intergovernmental processes.

Skill in strategic planning, program development, and organizational leadership; effective oral and written communication; researching, including data collection, statistical analysis, correspondence, public engagement and presentations; training and supervision of personnel;

Ability to lead, supervise, and develop management and professional staff across multiple disciplines; prepare and administer budgets and analyze complex data and policy issues; communicate effectively in writing and orally and to build productive relationships with elected officials, member communities, staff, and the public; manage programs and projects; interpret, analyze and explain federal, state, and locals laws related to land use, zoning, and environmental regulations.

Computer Skills

To perform this job successfully, an individual should have knowledge of spreadsheet, database, and word processing software, and must be proficient in Microsoft Windows, Excel, Word, and Outlook. Familiarity with GIS and the ESRI ArcGIS platform is preferred.

Supervisory Responsibilities

This position has full supervisory responsibility for the Tulsa County Development Services Department and serves as its department head. Carries out supervisory responsibilities in accordance with the organization's policies and applicable laws, including hiring, planning and assigning work, training, appraising performance, rewarding and disciplining employees, and addressing complaints and resolving problems.

Education and/or Experience

Bachelor's degree from a four-year college or university in Urban or Regional Planning, Public Administration, Geography, or a closely related field; plus, five to ten years of progressively responsible planning or development services experience, including at least three years in management or supervisory capacity; or an equivalent combination of education and experience. A master's degree and/or AICP certification is strongly preferred.

Language Skills

Ability to read, analyze, and interpret complex documents such as statutes, regulations, technical reports, plans, and legal descriptions. Ability to write reports, policies, and correspondence and to develop and present clear recommendations. Ability to speak effectively and respond to questions from elected officials, boards, member communities, staff, and the public.

Mathematical Skills

Ability to work with mathematical concepts such as statistics, percentages, ratios, and proportions and to apply them to budgeting, forecasting, and data analysis. Ability to interpret coordinate systems, scales, maps, and statistical data.

Reasoning Ability

title: Senior Product Manager - Safety
description:
Job Title: Senior Product Manager - Safety

Job Location: Toronto, Canada

Job Location Type: Remote

Job Contract Type: Full time

Job Seniority Level:

Veeva Systems is a mission-driven organization and pioneer in industry cloud, helping life sciences companies bring therapies to patients faster. As one of the fastest-growing SaaS companies in history, we surpassed $3B in revenue in our last fiscal year with extensive growth potential ahead.
At the heart of Veeva are our values: Do the Right Thing, Customer Success, Employee Success, and Speed. We're not just any public company – we made history in 2021 by becoming a public benefit corporation (PBC), legally bound to balancing the interests of customers, employees, society, and investors.
As a Work Anywhere company, we support your flexibility to work from home or in the office, so you can thrive in your ideal environment.
Join us in transforming the life sciences industry, committed to making a positive impact on its customers, employees, and communities.

The Role

As the newest member of our Product Management team, you will play a crucial role in advancing Veeva Safety, an enterprise-level pharmacovigilance (drug safety) solution that manages the intake, processing, and submission of adverse events for clinical and post-market products. Your contributions will enable the Life Sciences industry as a whole to better track and inform the public about the safety risk profile of the medicines we and our loved ones often rely upon for continued health.
The ideal candidate brings a strong work ethic, a highly inquisitive mindset, a knack for dissecting complex business problems, a collaborative spirit, and a positive attitude in the face of challenges. In this role, you will work closely with customers, plus our in-house industry experts and technology A-players to iteratively define a strategic road map, design & build elegant solutions, and bring rewarding solutions to market.
What You'll Do
    • Learn our industry and develop a keen understanding of our customers’ greatest pain points
    • Shape the product road map, prioritizing across releases with respect to strategic and operational goals
    • Design and specify accurate market-wide solutions for urgent real-world problems, in close collaboration with product development teams
    • Become the subject matter expert for your areas of product ownership, providing much-needed guidance to all internal teams
    • Drive product adoption, and measure the success of your solutions
Requirements
    • 5+ years of product management experience with enterprise software
    • 7+ years professional work experience in agile environments
    • Highly motivated, self-driven individual with a strong passion for product success
    • Proven experience with product design and road map planning
    • Excellent verbal and written communication skills
    • Bachelor’s degree in computer science, engineering, or business administration
Nice to Have
    • Experience in the Life Sciences industry
Interviewing with Veeva
We value your time and believe in a transparent hiring process. Here is the process you can expect.

title: Verzorgende IG Thuiszorg- Beeldzorg
description:
Houd je van zelfstandig werken, het contact met cliënten, maar wil je liever niet meer in de fysieke route werken? Dan is dit jouw kans en ga aan de slag in het beeldzorgteam van Florence!

Dit ga je doen

In het beeldzorgteam werk je zelfstandig, maar sta je er nooit alleen voor. Samen met het team, andere collega's in de wijk en mantelzorgers, zorg je ervoor dat cliënten veilig en comfortabel thuis kunnen blijven wonen. Je:

· Biedt persoonlijke zorg en ondersteuning op afstand.

· Houdt het welzijn van cliënten scherp in de gaten.

· Signaleert, rapporteert en denkt mee in oplossingen.

· Werkt samen met collega’s en andere zorgprofessionals.

· Draagt bij aan de verdere ontwikkeling van beeldzorg.

Dit ben jij

‘Op je plek bij Florence’

Bij Florence ben je niet alleen, met een grote groep collega's zoals jij ga je elke uitdaging aan! Zoals alle collega's die werkzaam zijn bij Florence, staat jouw ontwikkeling centraal. Of je nu net je diploma op zak hebt, midden in je zorgopleiding zit of al jaren ervaring hebt: jouw ambitie en talent krijgen bij ons de ruimte om te groeien. Juist omdat Florence zo’n grote organisatie is, vind je altijd een team of functie die bij jou past!

· Diploma Verzorgende IG (niveau 3) óf HBO-V student vanaf jaar 3

· Digitaal vaardig en affiniteit met zorgtechnologie

· Flexibel, zelfstandig en positief ingesteld

· Goede communicatieve vaardigheden (ook via beeld)

· Goede beheersing van de Nederlandse taal

· Je houdt van afwisseling en maakt makkelijk contact

Dit bieden wij jou

Meteen een vast contract voor onbepaalde tijd – wel zo fijn!

Je krijgt 8% vakantiegeld én een eindejaarsuitkering van 8,33%.

Ruimte voor vrije tijd: 237,4 vakantie-uren bij een fulltime dienstverband (36 uur).

We vergoeden je reiskosten met € 0,23 per kilometer.

Voor meer arbeidsvoorwaarden bekijk de CAO VVT.

Je kan altijd in ontwikkeling blijven. Florence heeft een eigen ontwikkelcentrum en hanteert een actief mobiliteitsbeleid.

Dit is jouw werkplek

Wij zijn een nieuw team en op zoek naar mensen die enthousiast zijn om hier een succes van te maken. Samen gaan wij zorg op afstand mogelijk maken voor thuiswonende cliënten in alle regio's waar Florence een wijkteam heeft, zodat er altijd mogelijkheid is voor inzet van fysieke zorg wanneer nodig.

We werken vanuit de locatie Gulden Huis in Den Haag en het is mogelijk om deels thuis te werken in de avonden en weekenden.

Solliciteren en extra informatie

Heb je interesse in deze functie? Solliciteer dan direct – we kijken uit naar jouw reactie!
Heb je nog vragen of wil je graag meer weten? Neem gerust contact op met Nancy van den Berg via 06-28111372 of nancy.van.den.berg@florence.nl.

title: Magnetic Particle Technician II
description:
Join our team as a Magnetic Particle Level 2 Technician, where you’ll perform hands-on inspection of customer materials to ensure quality and compliance with industry standards. This role involves magnetic particle testing, equipment setup, and documenting results, along with occasional use of cranes and forklifts to handle materials. Ideal candidates are detail-oriented, safety-minded, and enjoy working in a collaborative, fast-paced environment.

This role involves working at our location in Hatfield PA, Monday through Thursday from 6am to 4:30pm.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Performs magnetic particle testing of parts and materials as assigned by the MP Supervisor, Lead MP Technician, or the NDT Manager.
  • Handles materials utilizing monorail cranes and forklifts as needed.
  • Unpacks materials received for testing and repackages the materials for shipping after testing has been completed as needed.
  • Follows all applicable and required specifications and procedures, ensuring accuracy and compliance to all test requirements.
  • Ensures that the test equipment and instruments are functioning properly, and calibration is valid prior to performing any tests. Informs the MP Supervisor whenever any equipment is found to be out of calibration or in need of repair.
  • Analyzes and documents test results, consulting with the MP Supervisor, MP Lead Technician, or MP Level 3 as necessary.
  • Monitors ever changing scheduled completion dates and times to insure that established schedules are met. The MP Supervisor must be notified sufficiently in advance whenever the schedule for a job might not be met.
  • Assists with maintaining test equipment. This includes cleaning the equipment, performing preventive maintenance as scheduled, and performing repair maintenance as required.
    • Maintains assigned work area(s) in a clean, organized, and safe condition.
    • Understands and complies with LTI’s QA Program.
    • Seeks clarification from MP Supervisor, MP Lead Technician, or MP Level 3 when specifications or directions are unclear.
    • Complies with all company policies and procedures.
    • Follows all safety rules and regulations and utilizes personal protective equipment as required.
    • Performs other duties and responsibilities as assigned or directed by the MP Supervisor, MP Lead Technician, or the NDT Manager.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Sufficient experience to meet the minimum requirement for certification level required in accordance LTI’s certification procedures preferred.
  • High school diploma or general education degree (GED).
  • Computer skills required: Microsoft Office
  • Must have excellent attention to details, process work with accuracy, and be able to work in a team environment with minimal supervision.
  • Must pass an annual eye examination with J1 @ 12” visual acuity required, must be able to focus and satisfactorily pass both written tests and practical examinations, and must have the ability to resolve problems that occur during testing.
  • Must be able to lift 50 to 75 pounds.
  • Must meet citizenship eligibility required by accrediting bodies.

This position requires use of information or access to processes subject to national security controls under U.S. export laws including but not limited to International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR). In accordance with ITAR, to be qualified to work in this facility, applicants must be a US Person, which is defined as a US National, US Permanent Resident, and certain categories of Asylees and Refugees.

LTI is the recipient of the Top Workplaces Award by the Philadelphia Inquirer and offers a full and comprehensive benefit package which includes Health, dental, 401k with company match, LTD, STD, Company Paid Holidays, Paid Time Off (PTO), advancement opportunities, and more!

title: Non-Destructive Testing Tool Inspector, Level 1
description:
Role Overview

The NDI Technician - FPI Level I performs fluorescent penetrant inspection (FPI/PT) activities on aerospace hardware in accordance with approved work instructions, applicable specifications, and Beehive Industries' NDT written practice. This role processes and prepares parts, performs required equipment and system checks, documents inspection results, and works under the guidance or supervision of qualified Level II or Level III personnel as required by NAS 410.


What You’ll Do...

  • Perform fluorescent penetrant inspection (FPI/PT) processing in accordance with approved work instructions, procedures, drawings, and applicable customer or industry requirements.
  • Prepare parts for inspection and complete required pre-cleaning, penetrant application, dwell, removal, developer application, inspection, and post-cleaning steps within approved process parameters.
  • Perform equipment standardization and required system performance checks using approved instructions; identify and escalate out-of-tolerance conditions.
  • Examine components under the required inspection conditions and accurately identify and document relevant, nonrelevant, and false indications.
  • Document inspection results, process records, traceability information, and required quality records accurately and completely.
  • When specifically authorized by Beehive's Responsible Level III and written practice, interpret and evaluate designated products or product forms for acceptance or rejection in accordance with approved work instructions; otherwise, refer evaluation decisions to Level II or Level III personnel.
  • Maintain FPI materials, equipment, work areas, and consumables in a condition that supports safe, compliant, and repeatable inspection results.
  • Follow chemical handling, PPE, UV-A exposure, environmental, EHS, quality, and foreign object debris (FOD) controls applicable to the inspection area.
  • Support internal, customer, regulatory, and special-process audits by maintaining accurate records and demonstrating adherence to approved processes.
  • Perform other duties as assigned in support of Quality and manufacturing operations.

You have...

Education

  • High school diploma or GED required; technical or trade-school coursework in nondestructive testing, inspection, manufacturing, or a related discipline is preferred.
  • Must meet, or be capable of meeting, the formal training, examination, and vision requirements for Penetrant Testing Level I under NAS 410 Revision 6 and Beehive Industries' approved NDT written practice.

Experience

  • For PT/FPI Level I qualification, NAS 410 Revision 6 specifies a minimum of 16 hours of formal PT training and 130 hours of applicable experience; documented prior training and experience may be accepted only as permitted by Beehive's written practice and approved by the Responsible Level III or Examiner.
  • Hands-on experience in aerospace, precision manufacturing, inspection, or special processes is preferred.

Skills & Competencies

  • Ability to follow detailed written work instructions, process specifications, inspection plans, and acceptance criteria.
  • Working knowledge of fluorescent penetrant inspection principles, process controls, equipment, materials, and common discontinuity types.
  • Ability to perform accurate documentation and maintain inspection traceability in paper and electronic quality systems.
  • Strong attention to detail, disciplined process execution, and willingness to escalate abnormal conditions or unclear requirements.
  • Ability to work collaboratively with Quality, Manufacturing, Engineering, and Level II/III NDI personnel.
  • Ability to meet applicable near-vision and color-perception requirements and maintain qualification status in accordance with Beehive's written practice.
  • The ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. government issued security clearance is required. U.S. citizenship is required, as only U.S. citizens are eligible for a security clearance.

Nice to have...

  • Current or previous employer certification to NAS 410 or EN 4179 as PT/FPI Level I.
  • Experience inspecting aerospace castings, forgings, weldments, machined components, or additively manufactured hardware.
  • Experience working in an AS9100 and/or Nadcap-controlled special-process environment.

Physical Requirements

  • Ability to work for extended periods in a manufacturing and inspection environment, including standing, walking, bending, reaching, and using inspection equipment and hand tools.
  • Ability to safely handle parts and materials consistent with site lifting requirements, with or without reasonable accommodation.
  • Regular use of required PPE and work around approved penetrant-process chemicals and UV-A inspection equipment; must follow applicable EHS controls and safety procedures.
  • Ability to work assigned shifts and overtime as business needs require; limited travel may be required for training or support at other Beehive locations


If this sounds like you, please submit an application with your resume. This could be the opportunity you are looking for to expand your skills, contribute to a winning team, and work with talented people who love what they do and take pride in our mission.


Beehive Industries offers a comprehensive benefits package that includes group Medical, Dental, Life, and Short and Long-Term disability coverage from day one. We also offer a generous 401(k) Retirement Savings Plan with a Company match. Every role at Beehive Industries is bonus eligible and will also receive equity in the company.

title: Plasma Processing Technician
description:
Responsibilities:

• Responsible for the evaluation of donor suitability for automated pheresis procedures. Administration and supervision of approved immunizations other than red blood cell immunizations. Provides limited emergency medical care to donors and staff, including the administration of medication or treatments in accordance with licensure or certification.
• Promotes positive customer relations with all donors.
• Conducts confidential and effective interviews with donors to obtain necessary information regarding suitability to donate plasma.
• In conjunction with the Center Medical Director and/or Center Physician responds to medically related questions from staff including donor suitability and provides information to staff on medically related issues.
• Performs medical history reviews and health assessments on donors. Assesses results of donor screening and laboratory tests to determine initial and continuing donor suitability.
• Notifies and counsels donors regarding reactive test results. Refers donors to community facilities for follow-up and counseling.
• Explains informed consent to applicant donors. This includes explanation of procedures, hazards and potential adverse events; explanation of immunization schedules, dose and antibody response; providing clear opportunity for donor to refuse participation; obtaining signature and date certifying informed consent.
• Handles medical emergencies at the Center by providing routine care as outlined in Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs); elevates situations to Center Physician or local medical service providers as required. Periodically checks emergency kits to assure supplies are present and in-date.
• Reviews test results and determines continued donor suitability. Follows SOPs regarding acceptable ranges of four-month required test (PE/STS) reports. Maintains knowledge of and apply all rules regarding four-month approvals and grace periods.
• Assess signs and symptoms a donor may exhibit that may result in the inability to continue donating.
• Manages employee hepatitis B and influenza immunization program, including administration of immunizations.
• Understands the policies and procedures associated with hyper immune programs at the center where applicable, and oversees donor immunization programs. Reviews antibody titer results as required. Maintains awareness of appropriate immunization schedule for each antigen.
• Ensures the accurate recording of donor data in the electronic donor information management system as outlined in the SOPs.
• Maintains clean efficient work environment, and ensures sufficient operating supplies and forms are available as needed. Follows all Health Safety & Environmental (HSE) and Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) policies and procedures. Promotes safety in all actions. May conduct routine audits of these internal procedures and documentation.
• Maintains confidentiality of all personnel, donor and center information.
• May be cross-trained in other areas to meet the needs of the business.
• Bilingual skills may be required, at the discretion of the organization, to meet the needs of the business.
• Perform other job-related duties as assigned.

Qualifications:

• Active state licensure from a paramedic, nursing, physician assistant, chiropractic, naturopathic training program or medical school required OR
• Completion of a foreign allopathic or osteopathic medical school and only if also currently licensed as a physician or certified as an EMT in the state
• Minimum of one (1) year experience in a health care environment or one year of clinical experience from a vocational or nursing institution
• Experience in a plasma or whole blood collection center or other regulated environment preferred
• Ability to make and analyze a physical assessment of heart, lung sounds, signs of drug use, etc.
• Ability to instruct donors, staff and community regarding the benefit of plasma donation programs

Different qualifications or responsibilities may apply based on local legal and/or educational requirements. Refer to local job documentation where applicable.

SUMMARY

New York Edge is seeking passionate and enthusiastic people to fill the role of Step Specialist. Step Specialists (Stepping or step-dancing) should have knowledge and experience in this form of percussive dance. They must be able to produce complex rhythms and sounds through a mixture of footsteps, spoken words, and hand claps. The Step Specialist should have experience teaching or performing in groups of three or more, often in arrangements resembling military formations. Additional knowledge in gymnastics, break dance, tap dance, marching, African and Caribbean dance, or stunts are preferred- but not required. Step Specialists should have good speed when stepping and experience using props such as canes, rhythm sticks, and blindfolds. Specialists should teach basic dance principles and go beyond through the act of demonstration. Students will follow, and the step specialist will challenge students to use their creative thinking in art. Exploring creativity is part of stepping. Step Specialists will utilize and adapt the New York State Arts Learning Standards and the New York Edge curriculum to create engaging activities encouraging participation in New York Edge programs.


ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS

  • Establish and enforce rules for behavior and procedures for maintaining order among the students for whom they are responsible.

  • Teaches the art of step, ensuring that each member is afforded an equal opportunity in learning the art.

  • Have the ability to understand and carry out instructions.

  • Organize performance groups and direct their rehearsals.

  • Establish clear objectives for all lessons, units, and projects, and communicate those objectives to students.

  • Ascertain and interpret group interests, evaluate equipment and facilities, and adapt activities to meet the student’s needs.

  • Prepare materials and classrooms for class activities.

  • Explain principles, techniques, and safety procedures to participants in the activities and demonstrate the use of materials and equipment.

  • Evaluate activities to determine if they are producing desired results.

  • Adapt teaching methods and instructional materials to meet students' needs and interests.

  • Progressive development of student skills leading to a final project



REQUIRED SKILLS

  • Must have knowledge of step terminology, history, and resources to develop a well-rounded and cohesive study of step dancing throughout the school year.

  • Must have knowledge and prior experience choreographing step-dancing and putting a performance together.

  • Prior experience teaching and instructing youth preferred

  • Must be able to follow a curriculum

  • Must be responsible, reliable, and punctual!

  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills are required.

  • May be required to walk up and down stairs.

  • May have to lift or move objects/materials as needed.

  • Work is performed mostly within a New York City Public School but may be required to interact with the community at-large during trips or events.



QUALIFICATIONS

  • High School Diploma or Equivalent required; some college preferred

  • A minimum of one year of work-related skill, knowledge, or experience is required.

  • A minimum of one year of teaching experience is required.

  • Must have passion for New York Edge's mission and demonstrated interest in education and youth development.

  • Candidates qualified to lead instruction in more than one activity are also preferred.


WORK SCHEDULE

  • 9-15 hours per week.

  • Monday through Friday -- 2:30 pm - 5:30 pm



The Step Specialist will be required to report to the school building and interact with staff, students, parents, and school administration.

At the time of offer and acceptance, the job requires safety and security clearances through the Department of Education and Department of Health.

title: HRIS Systems Analyst
description:
Overview:

The HRIS Systems Analyst administers, configures, and optimizes Holley's HRIS and timekeeping systems, including integrations, controls, testing, and issue resolution. The role owns data integrity across HR systems, leading recurring audits and driving continuous improvement across processes, data, and systems, and exercises independent judgment in implementing approved changes. As part of the Total Rewards team, it looks for opportunities to simplify and automate, and partners with HR, Payroll, Benefits, IT, and business leaders to ensure system reliability, accurate data flows, and compliance with internal controls. Timecard review and correction remain with people leaders, with HR guidance and follow-up, and Payroll reviews timekeeping outputs for exceptions affecting pay.


This is an in-office position that can be based in Nashville, TN or Bowling Green, KY. This role is not eligible for remote work.


Key Responsibilities:

HRIS Configuration & Support

  • Administer and maintain the HRIS, including configuration, security access, and core system functionality
  • Independently review employee and job data transactions in the system, applying judgment to ensure records are configured accurately and align with policy
  • Analyze and troubleshoot system issues, determining appropriate resolution or escalation
  • Support system testing, updates, and implementations, including requirements review, test execution, and issue documentation
  • Serve as the owner and subject-matter expert for data integrity across HR systems, leading recurring audits, validation, and exception reporting


Timekeeping Systems & Payroll Systems Support

  • Administer the timekeeping platform, including configuration, access, interfaces, testing, controls, and issue resolution
  • Train leaders and HR Managers on system use, including timecard review and approval, and handle system-related escalations
  • Serve as the first point of contact for timekeeping-system and interface issues; route payroll calculation, tax, and garnishment questions to the Payroll Manager
  • Monitor system interfaces and data feeds affecting payroll; correct system-side discrepancies and escalate employee-level time and pay questions to Payroll or the leader


Reporting, Data Integrity & Automation

  • Build and maintain HRIS and timekeeping reporting, including system audits, data-integrity checks, and automated timecard-exception notifications for leaders, HR Managers, and Payroll
  • Lead recurring data-integrity audits and analyze system exception and interface-failure trends, driving corrective and preventive fixes that improve data accuracy across HR systems


Compliance, Documentation, & Process Improvement

  • Support compliance activities related to HRIS and timekeeping, including SOX controls and audit requirements
  • Create and maintain documentation for processes, system configuration, data definitions, and workflows
  • Continuously identify, design, and implement improvements to processes, data, and systems—including automation and AI-enabled tools—that reduce manual effort and improve accuracy
  • Safeguard confidential employee, pay, and personal data, maintaining appropriate system access and data-privacy practices
  • Perform other duties as assigned

Qualifications


Required:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Business, Information Systems, or a related field (or equivalent experience)
  • 3–5 years in HRIS, timekeeping, or HR technology support, including hands-on system administration and payroll data support
  • Strong analytical skills with advanced Excel and reporting capability (lookups, pivot tables, reconciliations, large datasets)
  • Experience leading system testing, data audits and data-cleanup initiatives, access controls, and root-cause analysis
  • Working knowledge of federal and multi-state wage-and-hour and timekeeping requirements as applied to system configuration and controls


Preferred:

  • Experience supporting an HRIS or timekeeping implementation, conversion, or major upgrade
  • Hands-on experience with ADP Workforce Now, ADP timekeeping, or comparable HRIS/timekeeping platforms.
  • Experience using Smartsheet or similar project management tools
  • Experience delivering automation or AI-enabled improvements in HR, payroll, or timekeeping processes
  • Experience supporting payroll and hourly populations in a manufacturing or multi-location environment
  • Experience working in a SOX-controlled environment

What Makes Holley a Great Place to Work


At Holley, we’re more than a performance parts company—we’re a community of enthusiasts, innovators, and problem-solvers. We offer a competitive benefits package and a culture that values both performance and people.


Benefits:

  • Competitive medical, dental, and vision coverage
  • 401(k) with company match
  • Access to Financial Advisors
  • Paid time off and 9 paid holidays
  • Education Assistance program
  • Company-paid life and short-term disability insurance
  • Employee discounts on Holley products, events, and partnerships
  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP)


Holley is an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to building a diverse and inclusive workforce. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, marital status, veteran status, disability, or any other legally protected status.

title: Senior Staff AI Architect
description:
Join the leader in entertainment innovation and help us design the future. At Dolby, science meets art, and high tech means more than computer code. As a member of the Dolby team, you’ll see and hear the results of your work everywhere, from movie theaters to smartphones. We continue to revolutionize how people create, deliver, and enjoy entertainment worldwide. To do that, we need the absolute best talent. We’re big enough to give you all the resources you need, and small enough so you can make a real difference and earn recognition for your work. We offer a collegial culture, challenging projects, and excellent compensation and benefits, not to mention a Flex Work approach that is truly flexible to support where, when, and how you do your best work.

The IT function works to accelerate business growth through ensuring that the company’s operations run efficiently and effectively, ultimately enabling the achievement of company goals.

About the Role

The AI Solution Architect is a senior technical leader within Dolby's AI & Business Enablement organization, responsible for shaping and advancing the company's AI technology ecosystem.

As both a strategic thinker and hands-on architect, this role defines Dolby's AI reference architecture, drives the roadmap for agentic systems platforms, and ensures alignment between AI, data, and infrastructure strategies. The AI Solution Architect plays a critical role in enabling innovation, accelerating business outcomes, and helping Dolby realize the full potential of AI across the enterprise.

This position is ideal for someone who thrives on solving complex challenges, influencing technology direction, and delivering transformative AI solutions at scale.

Key Responsibilities

  • Define, evolve, and maintain Dolby's AI reference architecture, establishing scalable standards, principles, and design patterns across business groups and functions.
  • Own the roadmap for agentic systems platforms, translating business objectives into actionable technical strategies, milestones, and implementation plans.
  • Design and implement cross-platform AI integration frameworks that connect AI capabilities with enterprise data platforms and infrastructure.
  • Guide the optimization of AI-related compute and token usage as adoption scales, continuously adapting architectural approaches to an evolving AI cost landscape.
  • Solve complex and novel architectural challenges by applying expertise across multiple AI and machine learning disciplines.
  • Partner closely with Data and Infrastructure teams to ensure AI solutions are aligned with enterprise architecture, data strategy, and operational goals.
  • Provide technical leadership and mentorship to AI engineers, agentics engineers, and cross-functional stakeholders.
  • Build and maintain strategic relationships with technology vendors, platform partners, and industry peers to stay ahead of emerging AI trends and advancements.
  • Support AI Governance and Risk initiatives by ensuring architectural decisions align with responsible AI, security, and compliance standards.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 8+ years of experience in enterprise architecture, AI/ML engineering, or a related technical discipline.
  • Hands-on experience designing AI reference architectures, developing agentic systems, and integrating AI solutions across platforms and enterprise environments.
  • Demonstrated ability to create innovative technical solutions for complex challenges where established approaches may not exist.
  • Strong understanding of enterprise data platforms, cloud infrastructure, and system architecture, with the ability to collaborate effectively across technical teams.
  • Excellent communication and influence skills, with the ability to translate complex technical concepts for business stakeholders and executive audiences.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with AI FinOps, including AI cost modeling, governance, and compute optimization at scale.
  • Experience evaluating and integrating emerging AI technologies, frameworks, and platforms.

Why Join Dolby?

At Dolby, you'll have the opportunity to define the future of AI within a world-class technology organization. You'll work alongside talented teams, solve complex challenges, and help shape AI experiences that create meaningful business impact across the company.

title: Inventory Control Supervisor
description:
About Company

1 Click Logistics, founded in 2018, is a third-party logistics (3PL) provider committed to delivering exceptional service in distribution, warehousing, transportation, and innovative logistics solutions. With locations in Sparks, Nevada; Sacramento, California; Dayton, Ohio; and Hagerstown, Maryland, we are strategically positioned to serve customers across the U.S. Our mission is to serve our customers, team, and community while fostering a unique, employee-centered culture.

Our comprehensive services include warehousing and distribution, retail and e-commerce fulfillment, and transportation management, all designed to streamline operations and reduce costs for our customers. Utilizing advanced technology, our web-based Warehouse Management System (WMS) and integrated Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) connect seamlessly with major retailers, ensuring transparent and efficient operations.

Our ability to serve some of the world’s largest retailers, including Walmart, Target, Costco, and Home Depot, reflects our commitment to quality and efficiency. At 1 Click Logistics, we prioritize our employees’ well-being, fostering a supportive and inclusive work environment that empowers our team to provide the exceptional service our customers expect and contribute positively to our community.

Job Summary

The Warehouse Supervisor plays a vital role in overseeing the daily operations of a warehouse facility. Responsible for managing and coordinating the movement of goods, ensuring accurate inventory management, and maintaining a safe and efficient working environment. Additionally, leads a team of warehouse personnel, providing guidance and support to achieve operational targets and deliver exceptional customer service.

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Oversee the overall functioning of the warehouse, including receiving, storage, picking, packing, and shipping of goods.
  • Monitor and track inventory levels to ensure accuracy.
  • Implement and enforce standard operating procedures (SOPs) to maintain consistent and efficient operations.
  • Collaborate with other departments to coordinate the movement of goods and resolve any operational issues.
  • Supervise and train warehouse staff, providing guidance, coaching, and performance feedback.
  • Schedule and assign tasks to warehouse personnel, ensuring adequate coverage and efficient workload distribution.
  • Foster a positive and productive work environment, promoting teamwork, accountability, and continuous improvement.
  • Conduct regular team meetings to communicate goals, objectives, and updates.
  • Address employee concerns, conflicts, and performance issues in a timely and professional manner.
  • Ensure accurate inventory management through regular cycle counts, stock reconciliations, and audits.
  • Enforce safety protocols and best practices to ensure a safe working environment for all warehouse personnel.
  • Conduct regular safety inspections and identify potential hazards, implementing corrective actions as needed.
  • Ensure compliance with regulatory requirements, industry standards, and company policies.
  • Maintain accurate records and documentation related to safety, compliance, and operational processes.
  • Monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) and warehouse metrics, such as productivity, accuracy, and order fulfillment rates.
  • Analyze data to identify areas for improvement and implement strategies to enhance operational efficiency.
  • Generate reports on warehouse activities, including inventory levels, shipment statuses, and performance metrics.
  • Present regular reports to management, highlighting achievements, challenges, and recommendations for process enhancements.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.

Required Skills and Abilities

  • Proven experience as a warehouse supervisor or a similar role in logistics operations.
  • Strong knowledge of warehouse operations, inventory management, and logistics principles.
  • Familiarity with warehouse management systems (WMS) and inventory control software.
  • Excellent leadership and team management skills, with the ability to motivate and develop employees.
  • Problem-solving and decision-making abilities to resolve operational challenges and implement process improvements.
  • Attention to detail and a commitment to maintaining high standards of accuracy and quality.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Proficiency in using computer systems and software, including MS Office Suite.
  • Knowledge of safety regulations and practices in a warehouse environment.

Education and Experience

  • High School Diploma, GED, or equivalent.
  • A minimum of two years of experience preferred.
  • Forklift certification or the ability to obtain one.

Physical Requirements

  • Periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer.
  • Standing and Walking: The role requires the ability to stand and walk for extended periods as to navigate the warehouse floor and moves between different areas of the facility.
  • Lifting and Carrying: Must be able to lift and carry heavy objects, packages, and materials, often weighing up to 50 pounds.

description:
Job Title: Senior Program Manager, Global Medical Affairs - Rare Disease & General Medicine

Job Location: Washington D.C., District of Columbia, United States

Job Location Type: Remote

Join Amgen’s Mission of Serving Patients

At Amgen, if you feel like you’re part of something bigger, it’s because you are. Our shared mission—to serve patients living with serious illnesses—drives all that we do.

Since 1980, we’ve helped pioneer the world of biotech in our fight against the world’s toughest diseases. With our focus on four therapeutic areas –Oncology, Inflammation, General Medicine, and Rare Disease– we reach millions of patients each year. Amgen is advancing a broad and deep pipeline of medicines to treat cancer, heart disease, inflammatory conditions, rare diseases, and obesity and obesity-related conditions. As a member of the Amgen team, you’ll help make a lasting impact on the lives of patients as we research, manufacture, and deliver innovative medicines to help people live longer, fuller happier lives.

Our award-winning culture is collaborative, innovative, and science based. If you have a passion for challenges and the opportunities that lay within them, you’ll thrive as part of the Amgen team. Join us and transform the lives of patients while transforming your career.

Senior Program Manager, Global Medical Affairs - Rare Disease & General Medicine

What you will do

Let’s do this. Let’s change the world. In this vital role you will support the development and execution of Medical Strategy for Global Rare Disease and General Medicine Medical Affairs teams, including Dazodalibep and olpasiran. This is a key role whose overarching objective is to drive the development and execution of Medical Strategy in collaboration with Medical Affairs Leads. In this vital role, you will ensure that key deliverables including medical plans, insights, budgets and goals are brought to completion. The Senior Manager is a cross-functional, collaborative role across global, regional, and local Medical teams and partners. You will identify metrics, progress, interdependencies, and concerns, facilitate resolution as needed, and keep the Medical Affairs Team aligned around its priorities.

You will lead cross-functional planning, manage project risks, and drive resolution of complex issues while aligning strategic goals across the broader organization.

Responsibilities

  • Monitor and communicate progress, adherence to timelines, and variance from plan to Medical Affairs leadership.

  • Facilitate resource planning, financial planning, and capacity assessments in partnership with Medical Operations, Finance, and functional leaders.

  • Conduct risk management, contingency, and scenario planning using a variety of project-management tools.

  • Support continuous improvement of Rare Disease & General Medicine Medical planning, governance, and ways of working.

  • Drive operational excellence and automation by applying approved emerging technologies, including AI tools such as Copilot, to strengthen Medical planning, reporting, and ways of working.

What we expect of you

We are all different, yet we all use our unique contributions to serve patients. The qualified professional we seek is a Senior Manager with strong program-management experience and the ability to work effectively in a complex, global matrix environment.

Given close partnership with USML, GMAL, and global cross-functional stakeholders, the Senior Manager must maintain working hours with meaningful Pacific Time overlap. Availability generally from 9:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. Pacific Time, plus flexibility for key meetings, business priorities, and global deliverables, is required.

title: Mobile Crisis Counselor/Clinician
description:
General Definition:

In general, under the direct supervision of the immediate supervisor or clinical manager, the individual is responsible for providing community-based crisis services that are aimed at the

prevention, intervention, and immediate stabilization of crisis events experienced by MH/DD/SA consumers or consumers experiencing emotional distress in response to a crisis. Examples

of crisis services shall include community crisis response and crisis prevention/intervention.

Performance Expectations (Quality and Quantity):

Each clinician will be assigned primary and secondary responsibilities, these assignments may change at any time depending on the need of the agency/department and at the direction

of the supervisor.

1. Shall demonstrate the use of knowledge/skill/judgment and provide 24/7/365 crisis management services that evidence quality, and performance, and meet the needs of persons

served and other stakeholders. Performance tasks shall include:

· Mobile Crisis Counselor/Clinician will be responsible for telephone triage for crisis calls received directly from consumers, families, and community, or through Partners Behavioral Health Management. Calls will be directed based on the need of the consumer.

· Mobile Crisis Counselor/Clinician will assist with daily, weekly, and monthly reports as directed by Mobile Manager

· Mobile Crisis Counselors/Clinicians will respond to all referrals and requests within the catchment area (Gaston, Lincoln, and Cleveland Counties) on a 24/7/365 basis. Referrals and requests can come from a variety of sources. Each consumer is required to meet the admission criterion that is outlined by the state of NC. Our goal is to enable individuals that are experiencing an MH/DD/SA crisis or distress to access a range of crisis prevention and intervention services in a timely and effective manner in the least restrictive setting. The right service, in the right place, at the right time.

· Timely engagement and response are required for each referral and request. Mobile Crisis Counselors/Clinicians will respond within 30 minutes via telephone and within 2 hours face to face.

· Mobile Crisis Counselors/Clinicians will be expected to respond to a variety of locations (i.e. consumer residences, hospitals, work sites, schools, jails, shelters, walk-ins to one of the PCC 24/7 sites, etc.) and are expected to meet the consumer where they are at; ideally in the least restrictive setting.

· Once face to face with the consumer that is in crisis, the Mobile Crisis Counselor/Clinician will conduct a crisis screening/interview process. Then after the assessment, the Mobile Crisis Counselor/Clinician will begin to assist in the transition planning process, which includes referrals to a variety of resources and levels of care. Mobile Crisis Counselors/Clinicians will spend a portion of their time with the consumer in crisis and create a crisis plan to assist the consumer in preventing future crises.

· Ideally a crisis event will be resolved within 24 hours of the event's beginning date/time, however, it is required that staff continue to provide necessary follow-up and transition planning until the consumer meets the criteria for discharge from Mobile Crisis Services. All efforts and interventions, including the discharging of the consumer from Mobile Crisis, must be documented.

· Mobile Crisis Counselors/Clinicians are required to complete documentation and service noting at all stages of the response. For each Mobile Crisis event, there is a required list of documentation that must be completed. All documentation is to be completed and meet all documentation and clinical standards within 24 hours from the event's beginning date/time.

· Under the direct supervision of a supervisor, shall utilize knowledge/skill to achieve positive outcomes and resolve the crisis with crisis prevention/intervention techniques.

· Crisis services shall be based on models/techniques that are considered best/evidence-based practice(s) as defined by federal guidelines, program service definition, accrediting bodies (i.e. CARF), the NC Division of MH/DD/SA, purchasers of service, and PCC policy/procedure.

· Accurate service and billing record documentation that communicates the service(s) provided and consumer progress. Documentation shall maintain compliance with PCC policy/procedure, purchaser of service requirements (NC Division of MH/DD/SA, DMA/Medicaid, CCMH/LME); and, accrediting/regulatory bodies (CARF and NC Statute/APSM rules). All Mobile Crisis Counselors/Clinicians shall maintain consumer Record Documentation to include (as applicable to the service rendered):

· Screenings

· Crisis Plans

· Authorizations

· Service Notes

· Other Clinical Documentation (i.e. crisis evaluation, financial forms, other forms as indicated by MCM Audit Form or by supervisor).

· Use of a community-based team approach that utilizes the resources of the community, consumer, and treatment team, to achieve positive consumer outcomes, stabilize the crisis and assist with arranging appropriate transitions for the consumer to needed services and supports.

· Treatment approaches could include assessment, individual/family counseling, process, and psycho-educational groups that promote the development of knowledge and skills related to recovery from substance abuse and mental health disorders

· The ability to effectively utilize clinical supervision to enhance professional growth and promote the recovery of persons served.

· Must meet productivity standards as specified by administrative and/or clinical supervisor.

2. Shall demonstrate the ability to work/be part of 24/7/365 organizational and therapeutic teams, and maintain positive working relationships with consumers, community stakeholders, referral organizations, and other employees/ departments of PCC.

· Based on the daily needs of the services provided by the 24/7 clinical team a range of clinical, administrative, and support services to assure effective care and programming are necessary and required. This position requires a high degree of flexibility and a willingness to take on several roles and responsibilities from day to day, at the direction of the immediate administrative supervisor and/or the clinical supervisor and in support of the clinical team.

· To be an effective clinical team member flexibility is essential, clinical staff may hold primary and secondary roles and are required to fulfill both; roles may change at the discretion of the supervisory team and/or with the changing needs of the program/agency. Onsite clinical coverage must be maintained daily (i.e. 24/7/365 Clinical staffing), which requires the clinical team to be flexible in their scheduling; scheduling occurs on a rotational basis and may include 1st, 2nd, and 3rd shifts, as well as weekends and holidays. On-call coverage may be an additional duty assigned by the immediate supervisor.

3. Shall develop a working knowledge of applicable organizational policy and procedure and demonstrate compliance. This shall include, but not be limited to:

  • Personnel policies/procedures
  • · Employee Ethics/Corporate Compliance/Consumer Rights
  • · Service record documentation
  • · Confidentiality/HIPAA
  • · Clinical Policy and Procedure
  • · Credentialing Bodies: NCDHHS, CARF, DMA, and Partners Behavioral Health Management

4. Shall attend assigned training and continuing education to maintain credentialing and privileging, to include, but not limited to:

  • · NC Credentialing as a Licensed Qualified Professional, Qualified Professional or Associate Professional.
  • · Obtaining credentialing as assigned by the Clinical Director of Crisis Services
  • · Required Training (NCI, CPR, First Aid, blood-borne pathogens, Consumer Rights)
  • · Adhering to the PCC Employee Code of Ethics
  • · Adhering to PCC clinical policy and procedures.
  • · Required 20 Hours of Crisis training as defined in PCC HR Training and Development Policy and Procedure (I-B-006)
  • · Attend any supervision sessions and group staff meetings as assigned by the supervisor.

5. Shall complete other duties as assigned by supervisor.

General Knowledge and Skills (will possess at the time of employment or will be expected to learn upon employment):

General Knowledge of the dynamics of MH/DD/SA behavioral health disorders (BHD) and their impact upon persons served and their families; the bio/psycho/social factors involved in (BHD); up-to-date principles/techniques (evidence-based/best practices) of crisis response, prevention, and intervention application to individuals possessing (BHD); the community resources available to persons with (BHD), to include behavioral health, social service, community services, and self-help groups; knowledge of billing and service record documentation requirements (NC Division of MH/DD/SA ASAM/IPRS, DMA/Value Options, CCMH/LME, and PCC policy/procedure.

General Skill in the application of crisis assessment/prevention/intervention techniques that are considered evidence-based/best practices as defined by the NC Division of MH/DD/SA, and/or literature/research, and organizational policy/procedure; skill in the delivery of services using accepted crisis treatment modalities, to include, individual, family, marital, and in-community; skill in establishing/maintaining effective therapeutic and professional relationships with persons served and/or their family members; behavioral health providers; and, skill in accurately documenting services provided and billed.

Qualifications:

Mobile Crisis Counselor I/II/III

  • At a minimum, the individual must meet the NC Division of MH/DD/SA requirements for Qualified Professional.
  • Bachelor’s degree in a behavioral science field from an accredited college/university and meet NC Division of MH/DD/SA Professional (QP or AP) credentialing requirements.
  • At least one (1) year of experience in delivering clinical Crisis services. Credit may be given for previous clinical experience in other job positions, practicums, and internships as this experience relates to the provision of crisis services.
  • CADC certification may be required for some positions.

Mobile Crisis Clinician II/III (licensure requirements)

Must be either fully or provisional licensed as an LCSW(A), LPC(A), LCAS(A), etc.

Additional Job Requirements:

  • Must have the ability to effectively hear and communicate with other employees, professionals, law enforcement, magistrate the public, and persons served.
  • · Must have physical mobility to respond and provide service in various community and onsite locations.
  • · Being on-call and shift work is required as part of this position with a team requirement to provide 24/7/365 clinical coverage.
  • · Must provide crisis prevention/intervention services in community locations including hospital settings, in-home, and other locations that are safe in the community. In-home crisis intervention may require an escort from law enforcement.
  • · Must have reliable transportation, maintain a valid NC driver’s license, and maintain adequate automobile insurance.
  • · Limited consumer transportation may be required when applicable and approved by the immediate supervisor.
  • · Travel is required as part of this position and may use the company-supplied vehicle and/or use of a personal vehicle with mileage reimbursement as defined in PCC policy/procedure.
  • · Must have the ability to operate a telephone, fax machine, and computer hardware/software.
  • · Requires superior writing skills, and the ability to compose a variety of complex and sophisticated professional documents, assessments, and reports. Requires the ability to comprehend and explain complicated clinical documents and professional literature.
  • · Willingness to work in a high-stress/risk environment that is driven by team performance

title: 6777 - Trading Card Specialist
description:
Trading Card Specialist
About Our Company
At Lids Sports Group, we don’t just sell hats — we fuel fandom. As the largest licensed sports retailer in North America, we bring sports, fashion, and culture together in more than 1,300 stores nationwide. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, Lids delivers premium, fan-driven products and unforgettable retail experiences.

Our stores feature officially licensed headwear and apparel from collegiate and professional teams, alongside top brands like Champion, Nike, New Era, Lululemon Athletica, and Mitchell & Ness. We’re also the industry leader in on-demand customization, offering in-store embroidery that turns everyday gear into one-of-a-kind statements.

From specialty concept stores for the NBA and NHL, to iconic clubhouse destinations for the Yankees and Dodgers, we create immersive retail experiences that celebrate the teams fans love. Through collaborations with brands like Marvel, Peanuts, and The Walt Disney Company, Lids continues to redefine how fans represent their teams — in style.
General Position Summary
The Trading Card Specialist serves as the in-store subject matter expert for all things trading cards and collectibles. This role creates a best-in-class hobby experience for customers by providing expert product knowledge, educating collectors, maintaining category integrity, and driving sales within the trading card business. The ideal candidate possesses a deep understanding of the trading card ecosystem, including sealed wax products, singles, grading services, authentication, live breaking, hobby market trends, trading card manufacturers, distribution channels, and counterfeit detection. The Trading Card Specialist is passionate about the hobby, actively engaged in the collector community, and dedicated to helping customers of all experience levels build their collections with confidence.
Principal Duties and Responsibilities
  • Serve as the primary in-store expert for selling trading cards, collectibles, sports memorabilia, and hobby-related products
  • Educate customers on product releases, card values, collecting strategies, grading processes, authentication standards, and hobby best practices.
  • Maintain current knowledge of major trading card brands and manufacturers, including Topps, Panini, Upper Deck, Fanatics Collectibles, Pokémon, Magic: The Gathering, and other emerging categories.
  • Understand and communicate the differences between hobby, retail, blaster, mega, hanger, and premium product formats.
  • Stay informed on current market trends, player performance impacts, product demand, chase cards, and hobby-related news.
  • Assist customers with questions related to singles, rookie cards, autographs, relic cards, parallels, inserts, serial-numbered cards, and graded collectibles.
  • Educate customers on grading services offered by PSA through Lids, including the submission and authentication process.
  • Possess working knowledge of live breaking, group breaks, hobby community practices, and major hobby platforms.
  • Maintain familiarity with leading hobby retailers and marketplaces including Dave & Adam's, Blowout Cards, Fanatics Collect, eBay, Whatnot, Goldin, and other significant industry participants.
  • Drive category sales through customer engagement, relationship building, product recommendations, and exceptional service.
  • Support merchandising standards, inventory management, visual presentation, and product protection for trading card merchandise.
  • Maintain awareness of highly anticipated product releases and execute launch day procedures to ensure a positive customer experience.
  • Partner with store leadership to monitor product availability, customer demand, and inventory opportunities within the category.
  • Foster a welcoming environment for collectors, hobby enthusiasts, first-time buyers, and sports fans.
  • Build relationships with local hobby communities and drive customer loyalty through expertise and engagement.
  • Participate in training programs to remain current on industry developments, product knowledge, and company initiatives.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.
Job Required Knowledge and Skills
  • Strong passion for and knowledge of the trading card and collectibles industry.
  • Understanding of sports card, Pokémon, and trading card game (TCG) products and terminology.
  • Knowledge of singles, sealed products, grading services, authentication standards, and card condition assessment.
  • Familiarity with hobby marketplace trends and pricing dynamics.
  • Understanding of live breaking, case breaks, repacks, hobby releases, and secondary market activity.
  • Ability to identify common signs of counterfeit, altered, trimmed, or otherwise fraudulent cards and products.
  • Working knowledge of major hobby retailers, distributors, grading companies, and online marketplaces.
  • Knowledge of current athletes, prospects, legends, teams, and hobby-relevant storylines across professional and collegiate sports
Preferred Qualifications
  • High school diploma or equivalent required.
  • 1-3 years of experience in trading card retail, collectibles, sports memorabilia, hobby shops, card shows, live breaking operations, or related environments preferred.
  • Personal involvement in the collecting hobby strongly preferred.
  • Experience buying, selling, trading, grading, or evaluating trading cards preferred.
  • Familiarity with industry tools and platforms such as PSA, Beckett, SGC, eBay, Whatnot, Fanatics Collect, Dave & Adam's, and major hobby marketplaces preferred.
What We Offer
  • Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage
  • Retirement plan
  • 100% employer-paid benefits, including short-term and long-term disability, life and AD&D insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program
  • Paid Time Off
  • Generous employee discount and exclusive perks
  • Ongoing career development, including discounted secondary education courses
  • A collaborative, innovative, and team-oriented work environment
  • Early Wage Access options to provide added financial flexibility
  • Uncapped monthly bonus potential
Physical Demands & Requirements

  • Ability to occasionally climb a ladder and work with hands overhead.
  • Ability to constantly stand on shift.
  • Ability to frequently walk on shift.
  • Ability to frequently hear and communicate verbally with customers, employees, and other personnel.

  • Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these essential functions. For inquiries related to reasonable accommodations, please contact HR@Lids.com

Reports to Store Manager

title: Stormwater Inspector
description:
Performs a variety of routine and complex technical work inspecting storm water projects to ensure compliance with Federal, State, and City storm water codes and ordinances.

Job Responsibilities:

  • Manages and oversees construction sites related to enforcement area.
  • Enforces federal, state, and City codes and local ordinances; issues correction notices and citations.
  • Performs onsite inspections to ensure erosion and sediment control; prevents illicit discharge into drains, ditches, or open waterways; and prevents illicit connections between storm drains and sanitary sewers.
  • Conducts final plat walks.
  • Maintains records of inspection activities, and completes related reports.
  • Assures appropriate action is taken to bring code violations into compliance by issuing warnings, notices of violation, serving court summons, and/or any other appropriate action.
  • Researches problems and complaints regarding construction and development projects and code compliance; responds to complex and sensitive stormwater compliance issues; acts with fairness; and maintains political neutrality.
  • Assists in resolving complex and sensitive customer service issues, either personally, by telephone, or in writing; maintains records and documents of customer service issues and resolutions.
  • Conducts formal surveys and interviews to determine needs for regulatory purposes.
  • Conducts title searches; gathers data from property record files.
  • Updates databases and maintains records.
  • Explains, interprets, and provides guidance regarding applicable codes within areas of responsibility to architects, engineers, contractors, developers, members of the public, and other interested parties.
  • Responds to citizen complaints.
  • Conducts comprehensive screening on stream outfalls by walking the lines and outfalls; conducts testing as may be required to identify and remediate violations.
  • Maintains up-to-date knowledge of all job related codes and ordinances.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.

Education and Experience:

Requires a High School diploma or equivalent; three (3) years of related work experience in public works construction projects, construction inspection, civil engineering, or a related field; or equivalent combination of education and experience.

Licenses or Certifications:

Requires a valid State of Georgia driver’s license.

Special Requirements:

Georgia Soil and Water Conservation Commission (GSWCC) Level 1A certification or ability to obtain such certification within six (6) months.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

  • Knowledge of federal, state, and local stormwater codes and ordinances.
  • Knowledge of field monitoring to detect illicit discharges.
  • Knowledge of sediment control designs and measures.
  • Skill in communicating, both verbally and in writing.
  • Skill in working with computers, word processing, and spreadsheet software.
  • Skill in processing field testing kits and detection devices.
  • Ability to interpret and work from codes, technical sketches, drawings, schematics, and blueprints.
  • Ability to work well with the public and contractors.
  • Ability to read and understand ordinances, codes, plans, and blueprints.
  • Ability to work safely.
  • Ability to communicate effectively orally and in writing.

Physical Demands:

The work is medium work and requires exerting up to 50 pounds of force occasionally, up to 30 pounds of force frequently, and/or up to 10 pounds of force constantly to move objects. Additionally, the following physical abilities are required: balancing, climbing, crouching, feeling, grasping, handling, hearing, kneeling, lifting, mental acuity, pulling, pushing, reaching, repetitive motion, speaking, standing, stooping, talking, visual acuity, and walking.

Work Environment:

Work is frequently performed outdoors under various weather conditions; frequently exposed to vibrations; sometimes located near moving mechanical parts; and occasionally exposed to wet and/or humid conditions, wildlife, fumes, airborne particles, and smells. The noise level in the work environment is usually quiet in office settings and moderately loud in field settings.

title: Safety Patrol (Americana)
description:
Position: Safety Patrol
Department: Operations / Housing Program
Reports To: Program Management
POSITION SUMMARY
The Safety Patrol is responsible for helping maintain a safe, secure, clean, and orderly environment for members, staff, visitors, and the property. This position requires a dependable, alert, professional individual who can identify safety concerns, respond appropriately to incidents, assist with member intake and discharge processes, and maintain accurate documentation.
ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES
Property & Safety Patrol

  • Conduct scheduled patrols of the property, common areas, entrances, exits, parking areas, and exterior grounds.
  • Monitor for safety hazards, suspicious activity, unauthorized individuals, property damage, and other concerns.
  • Check doors, gates, and designated access points.
  • Report maintenance, security, and safety concerns to management.
  • Help maintain a safe and orderly environment throughout the shift.

Member Support & Accountability

  • Interact with members respectfully and professionally.
  • Monitor compliance with established program rules and procedures.
  • Respond appropriately to disturbances and member concerns.
  • Report serious or repeated rule violations to management.
  • Maintain appropriate professional boundaries and confidentiality.

Member Intake

  • Assist with maintaining a safe and orderly intake environment.
  • Greet incoming members and direct them through the appropriate intake process.
  • Assist authorized staff with intake procedures as assigned.
  • Direct members to their assigned rooms or areas after intake is completed.
  • Report prohibited, suspicious, or unsafe items or circumstances to management.
  • Maintain confidentiality of member information.

Member Discharges

  • Assist management with member discharge procedures.
  • Help maintain safety and order during the discharge process.
  • Assist with securing vacated rooms or assigned spaces.
  • Assist with the return of program property, keys, access cards, or other issued items.
  • Report abandoned belongings or property left behind.
  • Immediately notify management of any conflict, refusal to leave, threat, or other safety concern.

Incident Response & Documentation

  • Respond promptly to safety concerns, disturbances, emergencies, and calls for assistance.
  • Contact emergency services when appropriate and according to program procedures.
  • Complete a detailed and accurate incident report for all reportable incidents.
  • Document the date, time, location, individuals involved, actions taken, and management notifications.
  • Maintain objective, factual, and professional documentation.

End-of-Shift Reporting

  • Complete a comprehensive End-of-Shift Report before leaving the property.
  • Document patrols completed, incidents, member concerns, intakes, discharges, maintenance issues, safety concerns, and other significant events.
  • Identify unresolved issues requiring follow-up.
  • Communicate important information to the incoming shift and/or supervisor.
  • Ensure all required documentation is completed and submitted before clocking out.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • High school diploma or equivalent preferred.
  • Previous experience in housing, shelter, residential programs, security, customer service, or a related field preferred.
  • Ability to remain calm and professional during challenging situations.
  • Strong observation and communication skills.
  • Ability to complete detailed written documentation.
  • Reliable attendance and punctuality.
  • Ability to follow program policies and management directives.
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality and professional boundaries.

IMPORTANT EXPECTATIONS
The Safety Patrol must remain alert, professional, and attentive throughout the entire shift. Sleeping while on duty, failing to complete required reports, neglecting assigned patrols, or failing to report significant safety concerns may result in corrective action in accordance with company policy.
Safety Patrol staff are not law enforcement officers and must operate within the authority provided by the program, applicable law, and their training.
